Moreover, we propose that kink and antikink solitons could mediate coupling between occupied quantum states in the microtubules and thereby contribute to pattern formation in neural networks. This mechanism may well be what gives the brain the flexibility to support complex thought and other cognitive functions.
papers.comment: 38 pages, 11 numbered figures and 1 unnumbered illustration

papers.title: SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs
papers.summary: Agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that think with images interleave reasoning with zoom-in tool calls. However, this sequential loop is slow, and its answers carry no reliability score. Prior speculation of tokens, reasoning steps, or answers keeps the loop, and answer speculation also accepts confident errors. We find that the loop mostly adds one zoom-in step, with which a small model is ahead of the agent on most splits. Our key insight is to speculate the agent's next observation, which, unlike a drafted answer, can be verified, corrected, and used to test the answer. We propose SpecLook, a training-free speculate-and-verify framework with three levels. A small model drafts a glimpse and re-answers from it, and the question ends if the answer is unchanged and confident. Otherwise, the agent's large model verifies and corrects the glimpse without tools, and their answers are fused. Only questions that still lack evidence reach the agent, in one forward pass that SpecLook-Fast skips, so no question runs the loop. The trace scores every answer's reliability without labels. Extensive experiments on V*, HR-Bench, and POPE show that both are more accurate than every baseline on every split. SpecLook reaches 87.2% and 86.2% mean accuracy with 7.7x and 4.7x speedups over the DeepEyes-7B and Thyme-RL agents, and SpecLook-Fast reaches 9.9x and 6.3x.

papers.title: Formal Adequacy Index (based on Polish-language material)
papers.summary: Linguistic formality is one of the dimensions of stylistic variation in speech; however, simply measuring its level does not allow us to determine whether the chosen mode of communication is appropriate in a given situation. The aim of this article is to present the concept of a formal adequacy index (based on Polish-language material), which enables a quantitative assessment of how well the formality of a text matches the expectations arising from the communicative context. The proposed approach is based on the separate modelling of observed formality, determined on the basis of the linguistic features of the text, and expected formality, determined on the basis of the characteristics of the communicative situation. Adequacy is assessed by comparing these two measures, taking into account contextual tolerance thresholds, which may differ for a lack of formality and an excess of formality. The potential applications of the index are illustrated by an analysis of Polish-language emails containing apologies for being late, written by human language users or generated by a large language model. The implementation presented here is preliminary in nature and requires further calibration and empirical validation. The main contribution of this article is the proposal of a general methodological framework for the quantitative study of formal adequacy in various communicative contexts.

papers.title: Analytic guiding center formulas for bounce-transit motion in a concentric circular, finite inverse aspect ratio tokamak geometry
papers.summary: Bounce-transit motion in concentric circular magnetic geometry is typically analyzed in the limit that the inverse aspect ratio, $\varepsilon$, is small. We prove that this approximation is not necessary to study a concentric circular geometry by deriving new analytical formulas while retaining a non-zero $\varepsilon.$ We use these formulas to demonstrate that the approximation is robust for $\varepsilon \lesssim 0.3.$
papers.comment: Version of record, posted with permission of AIP Publishing, 14 pages

papers.title: Graphene Transfer for Vertical Amorphous-Selenium Photodetectors: Fabrication, Optical Transmission and Operation at 77 K
papers.summary: Graphene can serve as a VUV transparent electrode in vertical photodetector devices. Using an optically transparent graphene as a top-electrode of amorphous selenium (a-Se) photoconductor requires transfer process compatible with the thermal and chemical sensitivities of a-Se thin films. The baking and polymer-removal steps of conventional commercial Trivial Transfer graphene procedures are undesirable because heating can promote selenium crystallization and prolonged solvent exposure can cause delamination. We implement two alternatives: PMMA-free transfer of nominal 50-layer graphene and transfer of nominal 10-layer graphene using an approximately 80 nm PMMA support removed in acetone at 40C. Raman G and 2D bands identify graphene after transfer. Separate graphene/MgF2 specimens are characterized by dark-corrected transmission measurements over 120-325 nm and compared with earlier single-layer and nominal 6-8-layer Trivial Transfer spectra. The completed graphene/a-Se/Cr devices produce bias-dependent voltage transients under pulsed 415 nm illumination at 293 K and 77 K. These results establish an a-Se-compatible fabrication route for graphene-electrode devices and demonstrate vertical device operation at both room and cryogenic temperatures. The completed devices provide a platform for detection-efficiency studies, and direct VUV photoresponse measurements now underway.

papers.title: Reliability by Architecture: Agentic Workflows for Validated Multi-Physics Simulation from Natural Language
papers.summary: Preparing, executing, and validating strongly coupled multi-physics simulations require expert time. Agentic workflows use large language models (LLMs) to coordinate them from natural-language descriptions, but reliability requires checks of physical consistency and fidelity to the problem description. Our agentic harness implements explicit task allocation: LLMs interpret user requests and simulator diagnostics, generate input components not covered by predefined construction rules, and propose repairs, while deterministic routines construct supported components and check inputs, edits, and results. We evaluate CO2-storage problems using the multi-physics simulator GEOS, from compositional flow to flow-poromechanics with frictional fault contact. In 80 attempts on two flow problems, grounding raises the proportion of structurally valid inputs from 5/20 to 20/20, but acceptance reaches 20/20 only with complete rule-based input preparation. With identical inputs, local repairs correct three seeded defects while preserving valid inputs. Supporting tests identify simulations passing physics checks despite differing from the problem description or reference results.

papers.title: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion
papers.summary: The formation of compact stellar binaries requires rapid orbital tightening of their progenitor binary stars. This is theorized to happen via Common Envelope Evolution (CEE), when the stars orbit in a loosely bound, shared convective envelope, triggering an inspiral due to frictional drag. However, this inspiral in such a system has never been observed directly. Here, we present observations of AT 2025abao, a transient eruption in the Andromeda Galaxy, that originates from the CEE of a ~7M$_{\odot}$ asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star with its companion. Extensive pre- and post-eruption spectroscopy is best explained as a ~0.7M$_{\odot}$ companion inspiraling within the convective AGB envelope that powers a seven year period of gradual brightening - the first direct observations of frictional drag energy dissipation induced by CEE. The subsequent merger of the companion with the primary core within a few (<10) orbits powers the ejection of the outermost ~10% of the stellar envelope at speeds ~10x the primary escape speed, and empirically constrains the fraction of dissipated orbital energy available to unbind the convective common envelope, $0.01\lesssim α\lesssim 0.4$. This end-to-end characterization using multi-survey observations demonstrates a path towards mapping the landscape of CEE outcomes with upcoming surveys.
papers.comment: published online by Nature on Nov. 18, 2026 (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11221-z)

papers.title: QCCDCert: Formally Verified Compilation for QCCD Co-Design
papers.summary: Quantum charge-coupled device (QCCD) architectures enable scalable trapped-ion quantum computing by dynamically shuttling ions between specialized processing and storage zones. A QCCD can be built with many trap sizes and layouts. Comparing them requires compiling every program under each design's transport, capacity and control constraints, and trusting the target code of each compilation. We present a co-design framework built on one Lean-verified compiler. The hardware description and its operating rules are compiler inputs, so a single theorem covers every candidate design: the target code of every compilation preserves its program's behavior and obeys the hardware rules. Across 75 benchmark programs of 11 to 130 qubits, the best design found takes 66% less modeled execution time on average than the worst design of equal capacity. An AI agent that proposes devices based on our compiler's checked results beats the fastest of these designs on 71 of 75 programs. Our verified compiler provably avoids the 11 defects that we report in three previous compilers. It scales to hundreds of qubits, compiling 512-qubit programs for a 38-trap device in 1 to 29 minutes.

papers.title: Galilean invariance of Hamiltonian guiding center theory
papers.summary: Galilean invariance is a desired property for classical non-relativistic theories. Guiding center theory describes the slow drift motion of charged particles in strong magnetic fields. While one can guarantee a Hamiltonian formulation to all orders, it was previously unknown whether such a theory can possess Galilean symmetry. We show that specific first- and second-order guiding center models are Galilean invariant. Furthermore, we prove that one can ensure Galilean invariance to all orders.

papers.title: Laplace Bayesian transport maps for generative modeling of non-Gaussian climate fields
papers.summary: Transport maps provide a powerful framework for the generative modeling of complex, non-Gaussian spatial fields, such as those encountered in climate science. By mapping a complicated target distribution to a standard Gaussian reference distribution, they can serve as efficient stochastic surrogates. However, current Bayesian transport maps, which are modeled using autoregressive Gaussian processes, typically rely on empirical Bayes estimates that ignore hyperparameter uncertainty. Here, we contrast this point-estimate approach with a fully Bayesian model that provides posterior uncertainty quantification in transport map hyperparameters. To avoid the high cost of Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), we also propose a Laplace approximation to the hyperparameter posteriors, which can be computed at negligible additional computational cost relative to empirical Bayes. We provide numerical evidence and a real-data climate application demonstrating that these Laplace approximations can accurately capture most posterior summaries at a fraction of the cost of MCMC, while maintaining good predictive properties. Thus, our approach offers a scalable, uncertainty-aware framework for the generative modeling of non-Gaussian climate fields.

papers.title: Sub-Doppler Cooling of Potassium-41 in a Hybrid Quadrupole-Octupole Symmetry Magneto-Optical Trap
papers.summary: Sub-Doppler cooling processes rely on the near-degeneracy of the Zeeman sub-levels of the atom. Effective sub-Doppler cooling is only achieved when the ac-Stark shift of the molasses light is significantly larger than the Zeeman shift. This condition is typically achieved by switching off all magnetic gradients, and using Helmholtz coils to cancel Earth's magnetic field. Another way to achieve a nearly zero magnetic field gradient is to superimpose a second pair of oppositely oriented quadrupole coils with a different spatial geometry. At the ideal current ratio, this creates an octupole-symmetry magnetic field for the atoms. The resulting octupole magnetic field has a gradient increasing quadratically from zero at the center. In this work, the effectiveness of sub-Doppler cooling and trapping using D2 and D1 light is evaluated in such a hybrid trap for $^{41}$K. The temperature, lifetime, and phase-space density of the atoms are measured. For both D2 and D1 light, the octupole MOT is found to have a longer lifetime, while maintaining a similar temperature to the zero-field case. D1 gray-molasses temperatures down to $3.8(1)~μ$K and phase-space density up to $5.3(4)\times10^{-5}$ are measured for $14.3(1)\times10^6$ $^{41}$ atoms. The effectiveness of the hybrid quadrupole-octupole trap suggests the possibility of increasing the loading time for atoms into an optical dipole trap with active sub-Doppler cooling.

papers.title: Quantum Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport in spacetime through spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and spatiotemporal states
papers.summary: Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport is a mathematical framework that determines the most efficient way to transform one probability distribution into another while minimizing a given cost function. Its central constructions include the Wasserstein distances, which quantify the space of probability distributions, and dual formulations that link to convex analysis. Its standard quantum generalization replaces probability distributions with density operators and cost function with positive semidefinite cost operator, which should be regarded as spatial quantum optimal transport. In this work, we propose the quantum optimal transport problem in spacetime through the spatiotemporal phase-space Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distribution and spatiotemporal states and through spatiotemporal state. We show that the two formalisms are equivalent and related via spatiotemporal operator frames. In the Kirkwood-Dirac phase-space formalism, the spatiotemporal distribution and the cost function are complex-valued, and the spatiotemporal couplings are Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distributions that yield the correct marginals for the local states. In the spatiotemporal state formalism, the cost operators are generally non-Hermitian, and the spatiotemporal couplings are generally non-Hermitian and yield the correct reduced local states. The Margenau-Hill phase-space distribution gives rise to a real-valued optimal transport in spatiotemporal phase space; in the spatiotemporal state formalism, this corresponds to a Hermitian spatiotemporal coupling state. We give a rigorous definitions and a careful discussion of its duality. We also introduce a spatiotemporal quantum Wasserstein metric based on a metric in spatiotemporal phase spaces and show that it satisfies the metric axioms.

papers.title: Wasserstein Target Diagram for Model Evaluation
papers.summary: The target diagram is often used in geosciences, which provides a visualization tool for model evaluation and shows the temporal or spatial matching of data. However, its construction requires paired data of equal sample sizes, limiting its application to model comparisons involving unpaired samples or probability distributions. In this study, we propose the Wasserstein target diagram based on the 2-Wasserstein distance from optimal transport. Unlike the original target diagram, the Wasserstein target diagram does not require paired data of equal sizes and evaluates models from the probability distribution perspective. We further establish that the two target diagrams coincide when the given paired data are comonotone, which is common in climate science, such as cumulative precipitation and solar radiation. Through two simulation studies and an application to wind speed distribution fitting, we demonstrate that the proposed diagram can detect the probability distribution discrepancies that the original target diagram may not distinguish. The Wasserstein target diagram therefore lifts the model evaluation to the probability level and provides a complementary approach to estimating the agreement in probability distributions.

papers.title: The Barrel Imaging Calorimeter of the ePIC detector at the Electron-Ion Collider
papers.summary: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) is a next-generation facility expected to address fundamental open questions in nuclear physics, including the structure and dynamics of gluons in nucleons and nuclei. The Barrel Imaging Calorimeter (BIC) is the electromagnetic calorimeter of the ePIC detector, designed to meet the stringent performance requirements of the EIC, providing precise measurements and particle identification of scattered electrons, photons, and neutral mesons. The BIC is a high-granularity sampling calorimeter based on lead absorbers interleaved with scintillating fibers, complemented by pixelated imaging layers based on the AstroPix monolithic active pixel sensor. This hybrid design enables both accurate energy and position measurements, as well as three-dimensional shower reconstruction, making it a key component for realizing the full physics potential of the EIC. The BIC has successfully completed its Preliminary Design Review last year and is currently progressing toward the Final Design Review. In this talk, I will present an overview of the BIC concept and focus on its current status and performance results from bench tests, system integration studies, and recent beam tests.
authors: for the ePIC Barrel Imaging Calorimeter

papers.title: Maximising the Open Magnetic Flux of a Star
papers.summary: We consider how to distribute the magnetic flux on a star's surface in order to maximise the proportion of open magnetic flux predicted by the potential field source surface model. The proportion of open flux is shown to be maximised by concentrating all of the positive and negative flux at antipodal points. For a typical source surface height, this enhances the open flux by 35% compared to a dipolar distribution. Even if the flux is spread over finite polar caps -- as on the Sun around Solar Minimum -- the open flux is still substantially enhanced compared to the dipole. Nevertheless, we show that the dipole approximation over-estimates the open flux for this kind of flux distribution.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS

papers.title: Folded out-of-time-order correlators in double-scaled SYK
papers.summary: Harlow and Zhao arXiv:2607.14215 have identified ``anti-scrambling'' as a characteristic signature of cosmological horizons in de Sitter space, and proposed that it can be realized in a quantum system with bounded energy by Euclidean time ``folding" of out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs). We implement this prescription in the DSSYK model. We use arXiv:2303.03474 to define an infinite-temperature ($β=0$) DSSYK OTOC that in the semiclassical limit of small values of the double-scaling parameter $λ$ reproduces the usual AdS eikonal shockwave behavior with its characteristic time delay, and then apply the Harlow-Zhao fold with the ``fake'' DSSYK inverse temperature $β_f$ playing the role of $β$. We demonstrate both numerically and analytically that the resulting folded OTOC displays anti-scrambling. The exact DSSYK evaluation tracks the semiclassical de Sitter eikonal formula in the scrambling regime, including a time advance instead of a time delay.The direction of the fold selects the side from which the continued eikonal amplitude approaches its branch cut. We show how our results are consistent with recent ``no-go" constraints. We compare the folded correlator with the two-shell analysis of arXiv:2607.14215: the growing term of the two-shell dilaton invariant appears in DSSYK with the same exponent, but as an imaginary part, while its real part, which would signal the backreaction that ends in a crunch, only moves by $O(λ)$ for thermal-scale probes. We also generalize to finite $β$; we find reasonable agreement with the de Sitter eikonal form for sufficiently high temperatures, but at lower temperatures the folded correlator is dominated by a pair of complex conjugate saddles, an anti-Stokes crossover that prevents retrieval of the eikonal behavior from the folded OTOC.

papers.title: Probing horizonless compact objects through observable signatures and images of accretion disk
papers.summary: The observed images of M87$^*$ and Sgr A$^*$ by Event Horizon Telescope motivate us to study the spacetime geometry and accretion flow dynamics around compact objects beyond the Kerr/Schwarzschild scenario. In this work, we investigate the properties of a steady, inviscid, axisymmetric, advective accretion flow around the Zipoy-Voorhees ($γ$-metric) spacetime by solving the relativistic hydrodynamic equations. The $γ$-metric is a static, axisymmetric generalization of the Schwarzschild geometry and is characterized by a mass ($M_\bullet$) and a deformation parameter ($γ$). We examine how the deformation parameter $γ$ influences the effective potential, the location and nature of the critical points, and the resulting accretion flow topologies. Then, using relativistic thermal bremsstrahlung emissivity, we compute the spectral energy distribution and bolometric luminosity of the flow. We find that $γ$ affects the luminosity in opposite ways for the flow having outer critical point (O-type) and that having inner critical point (I-type). Finally, combining the flow properties with general relativistic ray tracing, we construct synthetic images of the accretion disk for different values of $γ$ and observer inclination angles. The resulting observed flux distribution independently confirms the trends obtained from the luminosity and spectral analyses. Although the shadow of the $γ$-metric has been shown to be consistent with the observed shadow radii of M87$^*$ and Sgr A$^*$, its accretion flow topology, the resulting radiative properties and image differ from the Schwarzschild case, thereby giving a complementary way to probe the deviations from the Schwarzschild paradigm.

papers.title: Compute Before You Digitize: ADC-less Mixed-Signal Processing for Scalable Cryogenic Qubit Readout
papers.summary: We introduce DIRAC, an ADC-less in-cryostat qubit readout architecture that uses analog computing to redraw the analog-digital boundary. Directly operating on the front-end's analog output, passive complex mixers perform the equivalent of digital demodulation, ping-pong active-RC integrators average their outputs into down-sampled per-qubit traces, and a time-domain stage digitizes them, eliminating Nyquist-rate ADCs. A TX-RX co-design derives the mixers' local oscillators from the readout transmitter's baseband rather than per-tone PLLs. A per-line calibration flow trains the matched filter jointly with the neural network, improving fidelity and enabling low-bit-width, low-voltage digital processing. Designed in 22 nm FD-SOI and evaluated at 4 K on 1.12M experimental shots, DIRAC matches the fidelity of a floating-point (FP32) digital pipeline for readout windows down to 750 ns, at 31.6$\times$ and 238$\times$ lower energy than the fixed-point (FxP) and FP32 pipelines. It cuts the total 4 K power per physical qubit by 50.4% and 68.6% relative to FxP and room-temperature flex cables, respectively. At a fixed logical-qubit count and 4 K budget, this yields, against FxP, a code distance larger by 2 to 6 and a 1.6-7.3$\times$ (Willow) and 4.9-204$\times$ (SI1000, $p = 10^{-3}$) lower logical error rate.

papers.title: Mining the time axis with TRON. IV. MeerKAT detects a radio burst from a nearby M~dwarf
papers.summary: We report the detection of a minute-timescale, highly circularly polarised ($\sim100\%$) radio burst from an active M dwarf (spectral type M1Ve), PM J14111$-$6155, located 19.6 pc from the Sun. Identified in the 1.28 GHz SMGPS using 8-second integrations from the TRON-pipeline, the burst peaked at 7.7 mJy. Visibility-based dynamic spectra reveal a drifting, band-limited emission feature ($\sim$300 MHz FWHM) with a maximum cut-off near 1.65 GHz, associated with electron cyclotron maser instability (ECMI), implying the existence of large-scale magnetic topologies ($B_* \approx 0.59$ kG). A non-detection ($3σ$ upper limit) four hours later points to intermittent or rotationally modulated beamed emission. An analysis of both TESS and ground-based survey data failed to recover an unambiguous rotational period for the optical counterpart. Follow-up SALT spectroscopy confirms its active chromospheric state, exhibiting prominent emission in the Ca {\sc ii} infrared triplet, Balmer lines, and persistent double-peaked H$α$ emission ($44.6\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ peak separation) attributable to optically thick self-absorption. This discovery demonstrates that the coordinated use of time-series optical photometry, high-resolution spectroscopy, and high-cadence spectropolarimetric radio imaging enables direct probing of coherent radio emission from the magnetically active atmospheres of nearby M dwarfs.

papers.title: Gaussian Splatoms: Direct Atomic Structure Identification in Electron Tomography
papers.summary: Atomic electron tomography (AET) computationally reconstructs the 3D atomic structure of materials from a series of 2D projection measurements acquired at different tilt angles. Inspired by Gaussian splatting techniques from computer vision, we introduce an atom-centric parameterization for modeling AET samples. Instead of a conventional volumetric representation with a grid of voxels, we model the sample as a list of atoms, where each atom is a 3D Gaussian characterized by learned location, scale, and amplitude. The Gaussian model is a natural fit for atoms that allows us to easily incorporate prior information grounded in physics; we impose isotropy of atoms, a minimum interatomic distance, and realistic atomic radii. We show in simulation that our method is more robust than volumetric baselines to real-world imaging challenges, including a limited number of measurements and low electron dose. We further show that our method yields a more physically plausible reconstruction of an experimental 23,000 atom iron-platinum nanoparticle than a previously published volumetric reconstruction. Beyond tomography, our representation is a promising tool for any atomic resolution imaging modality (e.g. multislice electron ptychography).

papers.title: RummiAlgebra: A Polynomial Representation Framework for Game-Based Algebra Learning with Jokers
papers.summary: Connecting symbolic expressions to manipulable objects is a recurring challenge in introductory algebra. This paper presents RummiAlgebra, a design-oriented framework and browser-based prototype that maps a Rummikub-style tile-rearrangement task to polynomial addition, common-factor extraction, finite geometric sums, and context-dependent substitution. A numbered colored tile is encoded as a monomial c x^v, while a physical joker is represented by a distinct symbol J_i whose algebraic role is fixed only for a particular candidate arrangement. We define admissible polynomial forms for runs and groups and establish an inventory-conservation invariant. A soundness-and-completeness proof shows that physical-tile accounting together with the algebraic run/group templates characterizes valid final arrangements under the stated classroom rules; polynomial equality alone is insufficient. Four detailed examples illustrate decomposition, competing factorizations, one- and two-joker substitutions, and optimization as an optional extension. A targeted review distinguishes the approach from established Rummikub solvers, Rummikub-inspired arithmetic-sequence activities, algebra-tile manipulatives, and polynomial games. The prototype implements six small challenges and a separate rule-and-expression checker; their optimal scores were checked against an independent exhaustive reference enumerator. These checks establish agreement for the examples but do not establish learning effectiveness or novelty of the underlying algebraic operations. We close with a classroom sequence, assessment constructs, and a controlled evaluation protocol. The claimed contribution is a formally specified pedagogical correspondence and an interactive proof-oriented activity, not a new asymptotically faster Rummikub solver.

papers.title: Hebbian self-organization of monosynaptic reflexes in a biologically realistic multiarticular limb
papers.summary: Spinal monosynaptic reflexes depend on patterns of connectivity between muscle spindle afferents and motoneurons that should reflect musculoskeletal dynamics. One possibility is that the details of these circuits are specified genetically, but this requires an unlikely coevolution of musculoskeletal and neural elements. Here we show how biomechanical structure can determine the connectivity of self-organized spinal circuits. Using a neuromechanical model combining a multi-joint limb, proprioceptive feedback, and Hebbian plasticity driven by motor babbling, we find that biologically realistic connectivity emerges spontaneously when babbling is neither too sparse nor too frequent. This results in strong homonymous projections, weaker heteronymous projections among functional synergists, and very weak connections among antagonists. This outcome also depends on musculoskeletal morphometry. Heteronymous synergies form when proximal muscles are strongest---the characteristic gradient of mammalian limbs--whereas excessively strong biarticular muscles lead to unphysiological antagonist coupling. The mechanisms differ: homonymous connections arise from direct sensorimotor correlation during fusimotor coactivation by beta motoneurons, while heteronymous connections depend on multi-joint dynamics that emerge only after homonymous reflexes stabilize and increasing muscle strength generates multisegmental motion. Overall, this study provides a mechanistic basis for fetal sensorimotor development and generates testable predictions about the consequences of naturally occurring and experimentally induced variations.

papers.title: Minimax estimation for simultaneous deconvolution model in random design using wavelets
papers.summary: Simultaneous deconvolution model is investigated when the design points are random and follow bounded densities and errors are either $i.i.d.$ or long-memory dependent. We propose wavelet hard-thresholding estimators, and show that they achieve asymptotically near-optimal convergence rates for the $L^2$-risk when the response function belongs to Besov space under both $i.i.d.$ errors and homoskedastic, long-memory errors. However, under heteroskedastic, long-memory errors the estimator is not optimal. For the $i.i.d.$ errors, the convergence rates are {identical} to those found in simultaneous deconvolution under regular design {and $i.i.d.$ errors}. However, for long-memory dependent errors, the convergence rates are new {and completely different from those in simultaneous deconvolution under regular design and long-memory errors}.

papers.title: Plausibly Exogenous Instruments in Probit Models: Sensitivity Bounds for Average Partial and Interaction Effects
papers.summary: Sensitivity analysis for imperfect instruments usually targets a linear two-stage least squares coefficient, yet many applications have binary outcomes and probability-scale targets. We extend the plausibly exogenous framework to the control-function probit, targeting average partial and interaction effects. We derive the generated-regressor variance, union and local-to-zero intervals, and their asymptotic coverage under stated model and calibration conditions. A violation stated on the wrong latent scale can miscalibrate the interval by a factor set by the endogeneity correlation. Applications to Catholic schooling, sibling sex composition and Confucian clans compare probit and linear analyses. Stata and R implementations accompany the analysis.
papers.comment: 45 pages, 3 figures, 7 tables; paper and online appendix in one file. Stata and R implementations: https://github.com/jespernwulff/stata-apexog and https://jespernwulff.github.io/apexog

papers.title: Efficient interlayer interactions in non-planar molecule/transition-metal dichalcogenide two-dimensional heterostructure
papers.summary: Integration of molecules and two-dimensional (2D) atomic materials offer new opportunities for hybrid electronic devices. Most progress has focused on interfacing planar molecule. In contrast, incorporating non-planar molecules into 2D heterostructures remains challenging due to the three-dimensional orientations of ligands. Here we investigate interlayer interactions between discrete non-planar spin-crossover (SCO) molecules, [Fe(tBu2qsal)2] (FTBQS), monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), and hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) spacers through optical spectroscopies. FTBQS features bulk molecular crystal layers and can be mechanically exfoliated, enabling deterministic assembly of clean hybrid heterostructures. Robust photoluminescence (PL) quenching, even with an hBN spacer, indicates efficient Förster resonance energy transfer with a long decay distance. Gate-dependent optical spectroscopy further identifies charge transfer from the doping shifts in the TMD layers due to the TMD/FTBQS electronic band alignment. Our results establish efficient interlayer interactions between non-plana, discrete molecules and 2D crystals for hybrid electrical, optical, and spintronic devices.

papers.title: Bits, Not Boxes: Label-Free Layer Selection for Visual Localization in VLMs
papers.summary: Attention maps cheaply show where a vision-language model (VLM) looks, but attention sinks make them unreliable for localization. Contrasting the question with a generic prompt suppresses sinks, yet only some layers localize the queried object. Existing methods find these layers with box annotations or fixed rules. We show that attention itself can identify them. A question changes how much a head attends to the image and where this attention goes. The two effects separate exactly, and the second, measured in bits on unlabeled questions, indicates which layers localize. WhereBits turns these where-to-look bits into a layer prior and combines it with per-head contrastive scores. Its three design constants were fixed once on labeled COCO data, and a new model or resolution needs only unlabeled questions. Across eight VLMs, WhereBits matches the pointing accuracy of box-tuned layers on COCO and RefCOCO and ranks target tokens better. This advantage holds on a held-out model family and at higher resolutions. Its COCO pointing accuracy is 0.72, against 0.22 for mean attention. In training-free zoom-in, its crops raise V* accuracy by 6.0 points under forced-choice evaluation.

papers.title: Dynamics of a spinning body with scalar multipoles
papers.summary: We construct an effective worldline action for a spinning compact object in theories of gravity with massless, non-minimally coupled scalar fields. To this end, we generalize the standard skeletonized approach used in General Relativity to model the stress-energy tensor of a small body in a background spacetime, dressing its multipolar structure with the scalar field. Within a pole-dipole approximation, we derive a modified set of Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations of motion for the spinning body, together with the field equations for the scalar field and the metric. We consider both parity-even and parity-odd scalars. We tailor this formalism to model the evolution of asymmetric binaries, such as Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs), by systematically expanding the relevant equations in powers of the binary mass ratio and deriving the dynamics up to first post-adiabatic (1PA) order, along with the self-force equations needed to determine the particle's acceleration. For a parity-even scalar, the 1PA dynamics depends only on the mass, spin, and scalar charge of the secondary, plus a single self-coupling constant. For a pseudoscalar, we find that the binary dynamics coincides with General Relativity through 1PA.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Degeneracy and Distinct Horizon Geometries of Rotating Kaluza-Klein Black Holes in Independent External Electric and Magnetic Fields
papers.summary: We construct an exact finite-rotation solution of four-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory at the Kaluza-Klein coupling, immersed in independent external electric and magnetic fields. Exact algebraic balance identities reveal two distinct regular nonextremal branches with identical horizon area, quasi-local angular momentum, and electromagnetic fluxes. Under a common, explicitly specified reference prescription for the axial clock, rotational frame, and electromagnetic potentials, the two branches also have identical thermodynamic readouts, including energy, temperature, angular velocity, and electric and magnetic potentials. Nevertheless, the two branches possess nonisometric intrinsic horizon geometries, with every positive axisymmetric scalar-Laplacian eigenvalue strictly ordered between them. Thus, identical thermodynamic readouts do not uniquely determine the intrinsic geometry of a black hole horizon. We further establish that the exterior admits consistent asymptotic matching to two distinct exact rotating cylindrical backgrounds associated with its northern and southern polar regions. Their metric, dilaton, and electromagnetic fields become compatible in the angular overlap region, with uniform matching extending to both symmetry axes. Every regular noncritical exterior, including the supercritical branches, is globally hyperbolic.

papers.title: High-rate low-distance color codes
papers.summary: Experimental implementations of two-dimensional color codes encoding a single logical qubit have surpassed the fidelity of physical qubits. A natural next step is to investigate higher-rate codes that encode multiple logical qubits. Here we propose small, high-rate 2D color codes for this purpose. We design distance-$3$ codes with encoding rates up to $1/3$ and distance-$4$ codes with encoding rates up to $1/4$. We prove that these rates are optimal for color codes with only color boundaries on surfaces with non-negative Euler characteristic. We benchmark the codes by simulating Steane-style error correction with real-time feedback and no post-selection in a linear trapped-ion chain model with all-to-all connectivity. The two best-performing codes have parameters $[[20,4,4]]$ and $[[16,4,4]]$ and achieve break-even at two-qubit gate infidelities of $0.22\%$ and $0.26\%$, respectively. These results match the performance of Shor-style error correction with bivariate bicycle codes that use weight-$5$ measurements.

papers.title: LIC-Audit: How Comparable Are Reported Gains in Learned Image Compression?
papers.summary: Learned image compression (LIC) papers often report BD-rate improvements of only a few percent. They are measured against VTM reference software whose version keeps changing: the claims we audit name 7 versions, 5 in 2025 papers alone. But how comparable are these numbers across papers, and what evidence should future papers give for such small gains? We introduce LIC-Audit, an analysis of 353 released rate-distortion curves from 36 repositories, and a controlled re-evaluation of eight public codec releases with 28,193 encode-decode records. We identify three problems. First, different VTM reference runs change BD-rates by up to 3.56 percentage points, and on CLIC Pro published numbers order 10 of 55 method pairs differently from a common computation; comparing codecs directly over a fixed quality range removes this dependence. Second, releases use different and mostly undocumented conventions for counting bits, computing PSNR, and padding images. Under consistent measurement, the GLIC method's 1.00% lead over the HPCM method on Tecnick becomes a 1.43% deficit, changing only the padding reverses the comparison of HPCM and CMIC, and most gaps narrow when MS-SSIM replaces PSNR. Third, average curves hide how much results vary from image to image, so whether a small gain is statistically significant depends on the assumed variation. An optimistic assumption calls 12.0% of comparisons between equally good codecs significant on test sets as small as Kodak, instead of 5%; a cautious one leaves 18 of 45 differences between recent codecs undecided, yet per-image results show 12 of them to be significant. Beyond auditing past results, LIC-Audit provides a versioned evaluation protocol, a public leaderboard website with a scoring tool, source-linked benchmark data, per-image measurements, and reporting guidelines, to help future LIC papers make comparable and verifiable claims of progress.

papers.title: Experimental constraints on gauge hidden-variable models in Bell tests
papers.summary: Quantum mechanics assigns identical statistics to measurement procedures that realize the same final effect, irrespective of the transformations used to reach it. We test this operational equivalence with polarization-entangled photons by implementing one of Bob's analyzer settings either directly or through closed wave-plate trajectories $C_γ$ calibrated to produce the same measurement operator. Motivated by ontological descriptions in which a hidden frame is transported between contexts, we formulate a local path-memory model and derive the mixed-context bound $|S_γ^{\rm mix}|\leq 2+2p_γ$. The quantity $p_γ$ is a coupling-dependent counterfactual mismatch probability: it bounds a contextual Bell expression, but neither generates nor predicts the quantum Bell correlation. We therefore test path memory through the observable difference between direct and looped implementations, using a no-signaling phenomenological response in which a hidden holonomy $δ_γ$ modifies one correlation term in $S_γ^{\rm mix}$. The direct reference violates the Bell inequality, while the looped mixed-context curves remain indistinguishable from it within the experimental precision. Our results support the quantum equivalence of calibrated measurement implementations and constrain path-sensitive hidden-variable extensions that predict an observable memory of the optical history.

papers.title: Effect of scrape-off losses and current flattening on runaway electron dynamics in ARC
papers.summary: Disruptions in high-current tokamaks, such as ARC, may result in megaampere-scale runaway electron currents. In this work, we evaluate mitigation strategies via massive material injection, accounting for the combined impact of scrape-off losses due to vertical displacement events and current profile relaxation during the thermal quench. We find that scrape-off losses alone yield only modest reductions in runaway electron currents, but combining them with current flattening creates a beneficial synergistic effect. The latter broadens the current channel outward, shifting efficient runaway electron generation closer to the plasma edge where the dynamically contracting boundary can effectively scrape off the electron beams. This interplay significantly expands the operational window for mitigation toward lower assimilated densities, theoretically reducing runaway currents to manageable levels at experimentally feasible assimilated quantities.

papers.title: Orbital parameters for 50 million stars observed by Gaia and spectroscopic surveys
papers.summary: Together with ground-based spectroscopic stellar surveys, the Gaia mission has changed Galactic archaeology over the past decade. Nevertheless, attempts to combine these datasets remain scarce, even though precise orbital parameters for as many stars as possible are crucial to unraveling the Galaxy's formation and evolutionary history. This work aims to construct the largest homogeneous catalog of stellar orbital parameters ever compiled to date, using the most up-to-date data from nine large-scale spectroscopic stellar surveys (Gaia RVS DR3, APOGEE DR19, BOSS DR19, LAMOST DR11, Gaia-ESO DR5, GALAH DR4, RAVE DR6, SEGUE DR12, DESI DR1), combined with Gaia DR3 astrometric data and employing an orbital integration tool for orbital modeling. Our catalog includes orbital parameters, such as orbital distances, eccentricity, inclination, energy, angular momentum, and actions, for 52,423,233 stellar sources from Bailer-Jones distances, and 40,355,569 stellar sources from recomputed StarHorse distances, of which 41,100,866 and 30,777,133 are unique objects, respectively. We also included probabilities of belonging to specific Galactic components based on kinematic classification and chemical-abundance classification. Using this catalog, we recover the known kinematic substructures of the Galactic disk while extending their mapping to Galactocentric distances of $\sim17$ kpc, demonstrating the potential of the combined dataset for studies of Galactic dynamics and evolution. We expect that this catalog will benefit a broad range of research areas, from stellar astrophysics to Galactic archaeology.

papers.title: Qubit-qumode simulation of molecular torsion in photoisomerization
papers.summary: Photochemical reactions driven by large nuclear motion, such as the photoisomerization of retinal, depend strongly on both the global anharmonic forces of the potential and the periodic topology of molecular torsion. In this work, we develop a hybrid discrete (qubit) and continuous variable (qumode) quantum simulation framework for photochemical reactions that maps electronic states to qubits, vibrations to qumodes, and the periodic torsion to a compact qumode encoding. Applying this approach to the two-mode Hahn-Stock and three-mode PSB3 models of retinal photoisomerization, we compare i) local vibronic approximations, ii) the full trigonometric potential on the noncompact line, and iii) the same potential on the compact circle, which matches the molecular torsion topology. We numerically show that the topological description can significantly alter relevant observables. We realize the compact torsion via both a wrapped Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) encoding and a two-qumode circle encoding and introduce two methods that reduce the hardware resources of both encodings. Spreading an encoded coordinate over several qumodes lowers the average occupation number of each mode, and adding counterterms to the Hamiltonian reduces the required squeezing amount. We expect that these methods make percent-level simulations of the considered molecules promising targets for hybrid qubit-qumode hardware. For more complex molecules, each additional nuclear coordinate is represented directly as a single qumode or an encoded register using the same native operations, so the framework extends naturally to larger systems.

papers.title: Filling the interior of the light cone
papers.summary: The retarded Green's function of gravitational waves in a spatially flat Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker universe contains, besides the light-cone term, a tail supported inside the light cone. We formulate the tail, for homogeneous and isotropic backgrounds, as the solution of a ``\textit{Goursat problem},'' {\emph{i.e.}}, a hyperbolic partial differential equation with boundary conditions given on two intersecting characteristic curves. In this sense, we fill the interior of the light cone. We solve this problem directly in position space for any expansion history, and compare exact solutions in $Λ$CDM independently with a convergent double series about the coincidence point, and with an approximate analytic interaction model. We discuss the interpretation of the tail as the sum of the waves scattered off the background curvature, as suggested by its expansion in powers of the curvature potential. Our novel solutions allow us to follow the tail throughout the entire expansion history, from the electroweak epoch to today. We find that the tail of an early source records the trace of the cosmic fluid along the light cone, ordered in retarded time: single scattering accounts for its features in the radiation era, while multiple scattering is needed in the matter era. This work establishes the accuracy of our calculation of the tail and lays the groundwork for its applications. From the position-space data we obtain the large-$k$ expansion of the propagator. Its first correction, the effect of the tail, depends on the curvature potential integrated along the light cone. The applications of the tail, the power spectrum of a background of bursts, and the memory waveform of a single burst, both of which require convolving the Green's function with its source, are presented in follow-up papers.

papers.title: Symmetry classification of hyperfine rovibrational molecular phase space
papers.summary: Symmetry-based structures have advanced molecular spectroscopy and quantum information science, yet connections between these fields remain largely unexplored. We construct a phase space theory of a molecule by jointly treating rotational, vibrational, and nuclear-spin degrees of freedom as the quotient of orientations and normal coordinates by the molecule's point group. The various combinations of how these three degrees of freedom transform under symmetries organize a molecule's states into molecular species, and we show that each species is defined by a particular absolutely maximally entangled (AME) carrier state, or, for 45 species, by a two-dimensional space of them. Up to local unitaries and the order of the sectors, molecular species realize 21 AME states across 75 point groups: a product state, four maximally entangled pairs, and 16 genuinely tripartite states. A Fourier transform on the quotient relates orientation and angular-momentum descriptions while preserving these carrier states. We propose an example experimental protocol for preparing and driving symmetry-adapted bend states of $\mathrm{CaOCH_3}$.

papers.title: Tracking Representations in LLM Reasoning Traces for Iterated Games
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents achieve state-of-the-art performance across domains through chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. Despite their ubiquitous use, little is understood about the relationship between the externalized trace and the model's actual computation. We address this by investigating how LLM agents make decisions in iterative games with incomplete information. Using a series of mechanistic interpretability techniques, we find that the model forms and iteratively revises an internal representation of the game throughout the CoT. Once the model prematurely commits to an incorrect belief, it rarely recovers. This failure is manifested in both the literal trace and the layer activations. Ultimately, as multi-agent systems are more prevalent, our work opens the door to a more focused diagnosis of their strategic reasoning errors. For illustrative purposes, we offer an interactive visualizer of our methodology on selected sample traces at https://interp-self.github.io/gametrace/

papers.title: Separable equations of motion for spinning test bodies in spacetimes with Killing--Yano symmetry
papers.summary: At linear order in spin, the motion of a spinning compact body in curved spacetime is known to have two remarkable properties: (i) in Kerr spacetime, a suitable shift of the worldline maps the motion onto fiducial geodesics, yielding separable equations of motion; and (ii) in four-dimensional spacetimes admitting a non-degenerate Killing--Yano tensor, the dynamics are integrable. In this work, we generalize the worldline-shift method of (i) to the whole class of spacetimes in (ii), using a covariant construction built on the Killing--Yano symmetry. We show that spin then plays the role of charge: after the shift, the motion is described by a fictitious spinless particle, with charge set by the spin component along the orbital angular momentum, obeying a Lorentz-force equation. The effective field strength is built from the Ricci tensor and the dual of the Killing--Yano tensor. It vanishes in Ricci-flat spacetimes, recovering the geodesic description known in Kerr. In the general off-shell metric admitting a Killing--Yano tensor, we derive explicitly separated equations of motion, which reduce to quadratures and provide a constructive realization of the known integrability. Since no field equations are assumed, our results apply to any such spacetime, including those sourced by matter or arising in modified theories of gravity, and we illustrate them in Kerr--de Sitter spacetime.

papers.title: Generative diffusion models for lattice field theory
papers.summary: Generative diffusion models offer a new route to ensemble generation in lattice field theory. The backward, or denoising, process underlying these models is a stochastic process with a learned, time-dependent drift, which leads to a clear connection with stochastic quantisation. After reviewing this correspondence, I turn to theories with a sign problem. There the complex Boltzmann weight obstructs direct sampling, but complex Langevin dynamics can sometimes evade the sign problem by generating configurations on a complexified manifold, distributed according to a real and semi-positive distribution. This distribution is not known in closed form. I discuss how this distribution can be learned from complex Langevin data using score-based and, in particular, energy-based diffusion models. The latter give direct access to the unnormalised distribution itself, which can subsequently be used as the weight in a standard Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation. Results are shown for a simple quartic model with a complex action.
papers.comment: 6 pages, contribution to the Proceedings of XQCD2026, Busan, Korea, 14-17 July 2026

papers.title: ER=EPR and IMP wormholes in quantum gravity
papers.summary: We analyze and refine the ER=EPR conjecture by studying IMP (Isenberg, Mazzeo and Pollack \cite{Isenberg:2001qe}) wormholes in QFT and quantum gravity, in the AdS/CFT context. IMP wormholes are solutions to the Einstein equations constructed from another general solution of Einstein's equations by gluing a handle on a Cauchy slice with a constant mean curvature, so that the initial data on the slice does not change in the regions away from the handle. This is made possible by using what is called the conformal method. This same method also enables one to recover a well defined perturbation theory in quantum gravity, and particularly for asymptotically AdS spacetimes \cite{Witten:2022xxp}. Thus we construct the perturbation theory on these backgrounds in addition to exploring ER=EPR when $G_{N}=0$, in the limit it is perturbatively small and beyond perturbation theory.

papers.title: Lossless Reversible Watermarking for AIGC with Applications in Authentication
papers.summary: AIGC watermarking is commonly used for tracing, but it can also support applications such as authentication and tampering detection. We study lossless reversible watermarking, which enables exact recovery of the original watermarked image after permissible distortions. By exploiting the relatively low entropy of the information required for image generation, together with robust latent-space watermarking, we design a framework that preserves sufficient information for lossless recovery. We then apply the framework to AIGC authentication, which generally faces two key challenges. First, the authentication mechanism must resist adaptive adversaries. Second, the content relevant to authentication, such as visual designs or expressed messages, may depend on application requirements that are not known at generation time. To solve these difficulties, we incorporate cryptographic message authentication to provide unforgeability against adaptive attacks. Lossless recovery provides the original image as reference evidence, after which a suitable analyzer can be selected to make the authentication decision. Experiments on Stable Diffusion demonstrate exact recovery under a wide range of distortions.

papers.title: Twist-4 QCD Factorization for One-Point Correlators at Next-to-Leading Order in Electron-Ion Collisions
papers.summary: Energy and charge correlators have emerged as powerful, infrared- and collinear-safe (IRC-safe) observables for probing QCD dynamics in the vacuum, established within the leading-twist factorization formalism. However, their IRC safety and factorization properties in a nuclear medium, where higher-twist contributions are critically enhanced, remain unproven. In this letter, we present the first proof of next-to-leading order QCD factorization for one-point energy and charge correlators (OPEC and OPCC) in electron-ion collisions at twist-4. Working within the higher-twist expansion framework, we calculate the twist-4 power corrections to the angular widths of the OPEC and OPCC, and explicitly demonstrate that the IRC singularities cancel and fragmentation-function dependence reduces to momentum and charge moments for final-state medium-enhanced observables in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering. Supported by numerical evaluations, this framework establishes OPEC and OPCC angular widths as sensitive probes of higher-twist dynamics and fundamental properties of cold nuclear matter.

papers.title: Lunar laser ranging analyses of NGLR-1 data with PEP and prospects for MPAc: towards one millimeter range precision
papers.summary: Since 1969, Lunar Laser Ranging (LLR) has provided critical data for investigating Earth-Moon dynamics, lunar internal structure, and tests of General Relativity (GR). However, the measurement precision of historical arrays (such as those from Apollo and Lunokhod missions) is inherently limited by laser pulse broadening induced by lunar librations. To overcome this limit, next-generation single Cube Corner Retroreflectors (CCRs) of large optical diameter have been developed to eliminate pulse dispersion, enabling LLR measurements to advance from centimeter-level precision down to the millimeter scale. In this work, we present a detailed analysis of LLR observations from NGLR-1 (Next Generation Lunar Retroreflector-1), the first single 10cm-diameter CCR deployed on the lunar surface. Carried out using the Planetary Ephemeris Program (PEP), this study investigates individual range measurements, normal points (NPs), residuals, and observational dispersion collected by the ground stations at Apache Point Observatory Lunar laser ranging station (APOL), Wettzell, and Grasse. The results: demonstrate the success of NGLR-1 in significantly enhancing time of flight measurement precision compared to legacy Apollo and Lunokhod retroreflector arrays; indicate similar good prospects also for ESA's MPAc laser retroreflector (MoonLIGHT with Pointing Actuators) to be launched in early 2027; pave the way for a new era of LLR observations and enhanced tests of GR, alternative gravity theories in general and improved lunar geophysics and geodesy.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 14 figures, 1 table. Comments are welcome

papers.title: Scalar/axion Wormholes and Boundary Conditions in Gravitational Path Integrals
papers.summary: Recent work noted that whether or not a given class of spacetime wormholes contributes to the gravitational path integral can depend strongly on the choice of boundary conditions. In particular, for asymptotically-AdS scalar/axion wormholes with spherical boundaries it was suggested that there are regimes where the same wormhole contributes to a Euclidean low-energy effective field theory computation of the partition function $Z_N$ defined by imposing Neumann boundary conditions on the scalar/axion field, while it fails to contribute to a corresponding partition function $Z_D$ defined by imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions on this field. Here we investigate toy models of related wormholes associated with JT gravity coupled to a scalar field, asymptotically-AdS gravity coupled to an axion/scalar with toroidal boundary conditions, and asymptotically flat gravity coupled to an axion/scalar. In all cases we compare $Z_D$ and $Z_N$ as computed in a truncated low-energy effective theory by an appropriate integral over constrained wormholes. In each case we find that, even though $Z_D$ and $Z_N$ are related by an integral transform, the two generally receive contributions from differing sets of saddles. Along the way, we uncover a variety of additional interesting subtleties associated with semiclassical contributions to our $Z_D$ and $Z_N$.

papers.title: Are AGN Required? Updated Photoionization Models for Rest-UV Line Diagnostics in Reionization-era Galaxies
papers.summary: Rest-frame ultraviolet (UV) emission lines in galaxies provide important probes of the ionizing radiation, chemical abundances, and interstellar medium conditions. Here, we consider UV emission-line diagnostics for galaxies with the observed physical properties of young, metal-poor stellar populations in the epoch of reionization. We study eight $z \sim 7$--$9$ galaxies using deep JWST/NIRSpec G140M and G395M spectroscopy from the Carbon-3 plus Oxygen survey. We measure rest-frame UV and optical emission lines, $\mathrm{C\,IV}$ $λ\lambda1548,1551$, $\mathrm{He\,II}$ $\lambda1640$, $\mathrm{O\,III]}$ $\lambda1666$, $\mathrm{C\,III]}$ $λ\lambda1907,1909$, $\mathrm{[O\,II]}$ $λ\lambda3727,3730$, H$γ$, $\mathrm{[O\,III]}$ $\lambda4364$, H$β$, and $\mathrm{[O\,III]}$ $λ\lambda4960,5008$. The galaxies have low oxygen abundances, $12+\log(\mathrm{O/H})=7.50$-$7.90$, low C/O ratios, $\mathrm{C/O}=0.10$-$0.32$, and high electron densities, $n_e(\mathrm{C\,III]})=(1.9-4.9)\times10^4\,\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$. We compute Cloudy photoionization models using BPASS and BC03 stellar populations to test how lower C/O and higher gas density affect the UV diagnostics. We find that reducing C/O and increasing the gas density shift the star-forming grids into regions conventionally classified as composite or AGN-like. We therefore conclude that positions within these regions alone do not establish the presence of an AGN in the galaxies studied here. However, some lines remain enigmatic, including strong $\mathrm{He\,II}$, which is not reproduced by the updated models. These results highlight the need for UV diagnostic boundaries that account for the abundance patterns and gas conditions of galaxies during the epoch of reionization.

papers.title: Isotropic diffuse gamma-ray flux limits from Carpet-3 experiment data using neural networks with domain adaptation
papers.summary: Diffuse gamma rays above 100 TeV probe PeV cosmic rays and astrophysical neutrino sources. Their strong attenuation on background radiation makes the observed flux sensitive to the location of the emission and to possible modifications of photon propagation. Searches for an isotropic component require rejection of an overwhelming hadronic background, but uncertainties in air-shower physics, cosmic-ray composition and detector response can lead to differences between simulated and measured events. Here we report upper limits on the isotropic diffuse gamma-ray flux from 100 TeV to 10 PeV using 1078 days of Carpet-3 observations collected between 2022 and 2026. We identify photon candidates with a neural network combining the surface-array signals and measurements from the upgraded 410 $\mathrm{m^2}$ muon detector. Unsupervised domain adaptation uses unlabeled experimental events during training to mitigate the impact of simulation--data discrepancies on the classification. The limits are among the strongest available and provide benchmarks for tests of extended Galactic emission and modified photon propagation from extragalactic sources.

papers.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
papers.summary: Post-training quantization is the standard way to serve large language models at low cost. However, the best quantization recipe differs across models and precisions. As a result, experts must redesign it for every new model, which is time-consuming and often sub-optimal. Fortunately, an LLM agent can take over this design by refining the recipe over rounds of building and evaluating candidates, so that more rounds lead to better recipes. However, evaluating one quantized reasoning model takes tens of GPU-hours, and combining methods from different codebases means porting each to the new architecture by hand. We present QDA, a system in which an agent designs the recipe for each model and precision. To make evaluation fast, QDA scores each candidate in minutes by its output KL divergence from the original model on reasoning traces that the agent never sees, and checks promising ones with long generations to catch failures such as repetition loops. To make building fast, QDA provides a library of public PTQ methods that are compatible with one another and with new model architectures. Across four reasoning models, QDA improves accuracy over the strongest public recipe by 0.9, 1.4 and 2.2 percentage points on average at W4A16, W4A8 and W3A16, using 64 GPU-hours per search. On the 320B-parameter MoE model GLM-5.3-Flash at NVFP4 W4A4, it recovers 98.3% of the FP8 model's accuracy, against 96.9% for the best vendor checkpoint. Every QDA checkpoint also runs on existing serving kernels with no inference overhead. We will release the library, the evaluator and the harness.

papers.title: Optimal Joint Bounds for Sparse Ground-State Energy Estimation and Ground-State Preparation
papers.summary: Ground-state energy estimation (GSEE) and ground-state preparation (GSP) are fundamental problems in quantum computing. Given a Hamiltonian $H$ with $\|H\|\le1$ and a guiding state $|ψ\rangle$ with overlap at least $γ>0$ with the ground space of $H$, the goal in GSEE is to estimate the ground-state energy of $H$ to additive error $δ$ with failure probability at most $\varepsilon$, while in GSP it is to prepare a state with ground-space weight at least $1-\varepsilon$, given a gap lower bound $Δ$. Their costs are measured by quantum query complexity, i.e., the number of oracle calls needed to access $H$. Recent work proved optimal bounds $Θ(\log(1/\varepsilon)/(γδ))$ for GSEE and $Θ(\log(1/\varepsilon)/(γΔ))$ for GSP in the time-evolution and block-encoding models. However, these models do not directly account for the sparsity of $H$, measured by the maximum number $s$ of nonzero entries in any row or column. In the sparse-access model, oracles instead return the locations and values of these entries. This introduces the additional parameter $s$, and it remained open how query complexity depends jointly on $s$, $γ$, $δ$ or $Δ$, and $\varepsilon$. We resolve this by proving sparse-query lower bounds $Ω(\sqrt{s}\log(1/\varepsilon)/(γδ))$ for GSEE and $Ω(\sqrt{s}\log(1/\varepsilon)/(γΔ))$ for GSP, even for stoquastic Hamiltonians. We also show that these constructions recover the earlier time-evolution and block-encoding lower-bound scalings. We then give matching upper-bound algorithms in the reversible in-place sparse-location model. Thus, we obtain $Θ(\sqrt{s}\log(1/\varepsilon)/(γδ))$ for GSEE and $Θ(\sqrt{s}\log(1/\varepsilon)/(γΔ))$ for GSP, showing that $\sqrt{s}$ is necessary and sufficient and completing the joint dependence on all problem parameters.

papers.title: Chorus: Shared N-gram Embeddings with Layer-wise Adaptation
papers.summary: Language models can gain capacity at little computational cost from n-gram embedding tables: large tables of learned vectors for short sequences of consecutive tokens, which are looked up and added to the model's input or to its intermediate layers. Recent designs commonly use a separate n-gram embedding table for each layer, which makes the tables costly in memory and prevents layers from sharing what they learn. Sharing a single table, however, gives every layer the same embedding and leaves no room for layer-wise preferences, and it performs poorly in practice. We propose Chorus, in which one set of n-gram embedding tables serves the whole network and every layer reads it in its own way. Each layer maps the refined embedding through its own projection layer, after rescaling its components by factors computed from its current hidden state. Chorus matches the quality of existing n-gram methods with 87% smaller tables: with 1.2B table parameters it predicts text better than FactorEngram and DeepSeek's Engram do with 9.6B. It outperforms Engram, TN-gram and FactorEngram in every setting where we compared them, across table sizes from 20M to 9.6B parameters. We also show that the recently proposed memory-efficient optimizer Ember works well with Chorus, saving 99.2% of table-optimizer memory compared with AdamW without degrading training performance. These results enable further scaling of n-gram embedding tables along the table-size axis by reducing memory use and allowing shared knowledge to be reused across layers.

papers.title: Leading Axion Sensitivity with Interstellar Medium Optical Line Emission
papers.summary: We introduce interstellar optical line emission as a new probe of axion dark matter. Axion decays to photons or electrons can excite or ionize neutral hydrogen, producing H$α$ emission at a fixed atomic wavelength rather than at an energy set by the axion mass. Developing the formalism and applying it to the Leo T galaxy with Very Large Telescope data, we derive strong constraints for eV--GeV scale axions, covering new regions of parameter space for both axion-photon and axion-electron couplings. These results establish optical line measurements as a new discovery channel for axion dark matter, probe poorly constrained parameter space below hydrogen's ionization threshold, and constrain axion explanations of JWST's high-redshift supermassive-black-hole observations.

papers.title: Capturing Ultralight Dark Matter Around Black Holes
papers.summary: Ultralight dark matter (DM) can form hydrogen-like bound states around black holes (BHs), that can be perturbatively described at small gravitational fine-structure constant alpha=G*M*mu<<1, where M and mu are the masses of the BH and the DM scalar, respectively. We show that self-interactions lead to the formation of a 2p-halo around a Schwarzschild BH, with the final cloud density as high as 10^5 times the background density. We also show that for the case of a Kerr BH with a superradiant cloud, the decay of the 211 state can populate the ground state faster than it decays into the BH. Consequently, the 211 cloud mass is bounded from above by M_{211}^{crit}/M~=5*10^{-3}*alpha^{-1/2}*[f_a/10^{16} GeV]^2 up to an O(1) factor depending on the spin of the BH. Crucially, for rapidly spinning BHs with M~<4*10^6 M_{sun}, alpha~<0.03, and f_a~<9*10^{15} GeV the resulting superradiant cloud mass is lower than previously assumed, which might have an impact on axion bounds from measurements of stellar BH spins.

papers.title: Collective Superconducting-Qubit Interfaces for Microwave-to-Optical Quantum Transduction
papers.summary: Microwave-to-optical quantum transduction is essential for connecting superconducting quantum processors through optical networks. Mechanically mediated transducers, however, remain limited by weak electromechanical coupling, dissipation, and added noise. In this work, we study a transducer in which an ensemble of superconducting qubits couples collectively to a shared optomechanical resonator. For weak signals, we show that ensemble size and optical pump strength together set the conversion efficiency, added noise, and bandwidth, with pump heating limiting efficiency to a finite optimal pump strength. Near half excitation, the collective coupling grows nearly linearly with ensemble size, accelerating transfer of an excitation into the mechanics. We show that this speedup is offset by relaxation of the additional excited qubits, so the single-qubit coupling and lifetime still set the coherence requirement. Transferring exactly one excitation also requires an anharmonic mechanical mode, which an auxiliary qubit coupled to the mechanics can provide. In a lossless prescribed-Kerr benchmark with four qubits and $g_{\rm sm}/(2π)=3.81\,\mathrm{kHz}$, a mechanical anharmonicity of $100\,\mathrm{kHz}$ raises the final joint single-photon intracavity target probability from $19.6\%$ to $99.7\%$. Finally, we quantify the effects of decoherence, disorder, residual qubit--qubit interactions, and pump-induced qubit noise, finding that pair-dependent interactions reduce the optical retrieval efficiency from 58\% to 35\%. These results establish the coherence and selectivity requirements for collective quantum transduction.

papers.title: Fast X-ray Transients as Premature-Dissipated Gamma-Ray Bursts with Magnetic-Dominated Jets
papers.summary: Fast X-ray transients (FXTs) are extragalactic X-ray flashes with little or no accompanying $γ$-ray emission. We propose that FXTs and classical gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) share a common origin in Poynting-flux-dominated jets powered by the Blandford--Znajek mechanism. In this picture, FXTs arise when the kink instability triggers premature dissipation at small radii ($\sim 10^{11}$~cm), yielding low Lorentz factors ($Γ\lesssim 50$) and high compactness ($\ell' \gg 1$) that thermalize the emission into the soft X-ray band. When the kink criterion is not met, the jet accelerates to ultra-relativistic velocities ($Γ> 100$) and dissipates at larger radii ($\sim 10^{15}$~cm) as a standard GRB. This scenario can naturally explain the observed thermal spectra, low $E_{\rm peak}$, supernova associations, jet-break absence, and day-scale afterglow delays across five well-studied FXTs. EP240801a is explained as a boundary event, where premature dissipation does not exhaust the full magnetic energy; the residual energy is further dissipated at a typical GRB radius, producing the observed $γ$-ray prompt emission with an $\sim 80$~s time lag. A key observational prediction is that FXTs may exhibit $e^+ e^-$ annihilation line features sweeping from a few MeV to hundreds of keV within $\sim 0.01$~s.
papers.comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. Accepted for publication in ApJL

papers.title: Non-Perturbative Moduli Stabilization with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ Modular Symmetry
papers.summary: We study the stabilization of the three complex moduli associated with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ modular symmetry by gaugino condensation in $\mathcal N=1$ supergravity models from heterotic string theory, where one-loop threshold corrections fix both the modular weight and the singularity structure of the superpotential. We determine, for each threshold class, the complete parametrization of the consistent superpotential relying on Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ basic modular-invariant ratios and their syzygies, generalizing the insufficient SL$(2,\mathbb Z)$-inspired techniques based solely on polynomials of its absolute invariants. This structure supports a rich landscape of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua. Unlike in the SL$(2,\mathbb Z)$ case, higher-order zeros produce continuous surfaces and curves of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua, while, among the six isolated fixed points, only those with $S_4$ and $D_{12}$ residual symmetries can stabilize all three moduli. We also construct isolated vacua away from fixed points, some of which lie at the moduli values preferred by genus-two modular flavor fits, and examine the suppression of the geometric moduli masses near an enhanced-symmetry point.

papers.title: Melvin-type Electromagnetized Kerr Black Hole in Kaluza-Klein and Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion Theories
papers.summary: A naive application of solution-generating techniques to construct Melvin-type rotating black holes in the Kaluza-Klein (KK) theory in the presence of both electric and magnetic external fields generically introduces an undesirable Taub-swirling twist term. We investigate its origin and modify the electromagnetization procedure, thereby constructing an exact solution of the Melvin-type electromagnetized Kerr black hole in the KK theory without the swirling term. We also obtain the analogous solution in the Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion (EMDA) theory. The modified solution-generating techniques allow one to introduce both the dyonic charges and external electromagnetic fields independently into Ricci-flat seed metrics in both theories, without generating either Taub-NUT or Taub-swirling twists.

papers.title: The Holomorphic-Topological Poisson Sigma Model and Quantization of Affine W-algebras
papers.summary: We construct explicit deformation quantizations of classical principal affine $W$-algebras for every simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ using the holomorphic-topological Poisson sigma model of A. Khan and K. Zeng. A linear differential-graded presentation identifies the universal bulk with Chern--Simons theory near a principal nilpotent background, where holomorphic gauge gives a finite, 1-loop exact quantization. The quantum oper boundary observables form the principal affine $W$-algebra at level $k-h^\vee\hbar$; we also obtain this level shift directly for affine current algebras. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we prove a perturbative quantum equivalence between Chern--Simons theory and three-dimensional chiral gravity, including their oper and Dirichlet boundary conditions, and determine the quantum relation between their parameters.

papers.title: Horizon kinematics and the fine structure induced by finite-energy Hawking radiation
papers.summary: Hawking radiation can modify the horizon structure of a black hole through the loss of mass and global charges. Investigating this process through quantum tunneling, we develop a systematic strategy to reconstruct horizon displacements under finite-energy emission, even when their radii are not explicitly known. Inversion of the horizon condition allows to follow roots's displacements along sequences of static geometries. As a concrete realization, we consider a nonlinearly charged extension of the Bañados--Teitelboim--Zanelli (BTZ) family, whose horizon structure offers an ideal setup to explore this process. Of particular interest is an initial configuration with a double inner horizon coexisting with a simple event horizon. We show that neutral emission necessarily splits the inner root into two simple ones, revealing a horizon fine structure. For charged emission, the dependence of extracted charge on emitted energy determines the separation law and allows that preservation or later restore the degeneracy. We construct such channels connecting the same initial and final states through distinct internal histories sharing the same leading semiclassical factor. As emission continues, the larger of the newly separated inner horizons can coalesce with the event horizon, driving the sequence towards extremality with a vanishing temperature but finite tunneling probability. We find that zero temperature cannot be attained in finite boundary time while uniform adiabaticity bounds hold. We also establish a regime where the geometric expansion and the canonical thermal approximation remain controlled near this endpoint. Finally, applying this analysis to the sector reproducing a quantum-backreacted BTZ geometry reveals how the leading semiclassical corrections raise the temperature and enhance the neutral-probe horizon emission factor relative to classical BTZ.

papers.title: Seeing through the fog: astrophysical priors and the evidence for new physics in pulsar timing arrays
