Furthermore, we demonstrate the potential of this approach by comparing it with state-of-the-art methods based on Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs). We highlight that we achieve similar performance to that of IMU-based systems in highly dynamic scenarios and even outperform in specific cases of accelerometer measurement saturation. Finally, an additional experiment shows the potential use within a robotic system through the integration into an Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm.
papers.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, submitted to IEEE ICRA 2027

papers.title: Auditing a Learned Simulator for Legged Robots: The Robotic World Model on ANYmal D
papers.summary: A legged robot can learn to walk inside a learned simulator: a neural network that predicts the robot's next state and is run forward on its own predictions. They are usually trained and checked one step ahead, although a policy uses them for a hundred steps or more. We audit one published system end to end, without a GPU: the dynamics model of the Robotic World Model (RWM) for the ANYmal D quadruped, and the uncertainty estimate of its follow-up, RWM-U. We rebuilt the model to match the released code's outputs, losses and gradients exactly, measured 101 trained simulators, 200 compressed copies and 38 simulators of three other architectures, and trained policies inside simulators that we tested in a hand-built MuJoCo model of the robot. Training on the model's own rollouts beat one-step training at 368 steps on all ten held-out episodes (registered), although one-step training was better one step ahead. One-step checks therefore misjudge design choices: pruning 30% of the weights kept 90% of the model's skill one step ahead and 39% at 2 s. Ensemble disagreement ranked rollout error well (Spearman +0.90 at 100 steps), yet covered 4.6% of outcomes at one sigma, against 68% for a calibrated estimate, as each network's own variance collapses under the implemented loss. Two checks that need no recorded future ranked some pools of simulators well, but neither was shown better than 8-step error in a primary test. At the robot level, accuracy has not predicted walking: all 18 fine-tuned copies we tested predicted better than the released model one and eight steps ahead, yet 13 gave failing policies, and registered tests of whether any check ranks simulators by their policies were not settled. In a secondary test, running the authors' policy inside each simulator ranked them well. We also report nine of our own claims that we withdrew. Scope: one robot, one gait, simulated data, no hardware.
papers.comment: 39 pages, 13 figures, 20 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/joyjeet-singh/rwm and https://github.com/joyjeet-singh/rwm-robot-level. Extends arXiv:2611.02699 with robot-level experiments

papers.title: Nunchi: Ears Help Eyes in Multi-Party Conversations
papers.summary: Identifying whom a person looks at is central to understanding multi-party conversations, yet gaze geometry alone becomes ambiguous as more people appear. Conversations offer cues that geometry lacks, such as who is speaking and what is said, but no gaze dataset provides them for many multi-party scenes. We introduce SORBET, a benchmark of 3,340 samples from 1,578 clips with synchronized speech, transcripts, and attended person labels, covering more multi-party scenes than existing gaze datasets. Prior gaze models struggle to use these cues, which come in different forms, must be linked to the right person, and can conflict with gaze geometry. We propose Nunchi, a framework that constructs a text prompt from the transcript and the outputs of gaze and speaker models, links every cue to the candidates with shared labels, and lets a vision-language model (VLM) weigh gaze geometry against conversational cues to identify the attended person. Nunchi outperforms the strongest existing method by 4.8 percentage points. On SORBET, conversational cues help whereas additional visual cues do not, and the gains hold across three VLMs, with automatic transcripts, and on two existing datasets.

papers.title: Combining Pulsar Timing data with $\texttt{MetaPulsar}$. The linearized timing model
papers.summary: Combining the data of multiple pulsar timing array (PTA) collaborations increases the sensitivity to nanohertz gravitational waves (GWs) and other signals correlated between pulsars. The International PTA (IPTA) has combined such data, but historically these projects have taken many years. We introduce $\texttt{MetaPulsar}$, a software package that ingests the $\texttt{.par}$ and $\texttt{.tim}$ files of individual data releases, and turns them into single consistent deterministic models for the combined datasets, compatible with both timing packages $\texttt{PINT}$ and $\texttt{Tempo2}$. We validate the method in four ways. First, we show for two pulsars that the linearized timing solution of a combined dataset does not depend on the parameter values in the $\texttt{.par}$. A mild exception is formed by the Shapiro-delay parameters. No combination considered requires a manual refit. Second, for PSR J0613$-$0200 we show that the residuals are explained by the timing model if we take intrinsic red-noise and dispersion-measure processes into account, and that the single-PTA timing posteriors agree with one another and with the combination, except for the parallax. Third, we quantify the consistency of the timing parameters measured by different PTAs with a two-sample tension statistic, for every pulsar that is observed by multiple PTAs. Finally, we carry out a gravitational-wave background search on the direct combination of the NANOGrav 9-yr, EPTA DR1 (v2.2), and PPTA DR2 data releases, the constituents of IPTA Data Release 2 (DR2). The combined dataset is assembled in under two hours, and the recovered amplitude and spectral index of the common process are consistent with the published IPTA DR2 result. With $\texttt{MetaPulsar}$, a joint PTA analysis can be prototyped as soon as the individual collaborations publish their data, instead of after a years-long reprocessing effort.

papers.title: LUTBench: Benchmarking Text-Driven Photographic Look Transfer
papers.summary: Photographic color grading shapes the tone and color of a photograph to achieve a desired look. Text-driven photographic look transfer lets users specify these adjustments in natural language, with the goal of reproducing the requested look across photographs while preserving their content. However, prior research on text-driven color grading uses different datasets, text instructions, target definitions, and metrics. These differences make it difficult to compare how faithfully the methods reproduce the same look. To compare methods under a shared protocol, we introduce LUTBench. We collect 91 three-dimensional lookup tables (3D LUTs) and define one photographic look per LUT with a specified input conversion. Applying these looks to 5,000 MIT-Adobe FiveK photographs produces 455,000 input-target image pairs with reproducible target images. For each look, we use templates to turn measured tone and color changes on fixed color samples into candidate clauses. We use training image measurements to verify applicable clauses before composing the text description. The evaluation measures target fidelity, tests sensitivity to predefined input conversions, and separates generalization to unseen looks from reproduction of seen looks on new photographs. Across 16 methods, stronger text alignment does not guarantee target fidelity. However, most supervised variants improve fidelity on both seen and unseen looks.

papers.title: Event-Based Dynamic Lip Region Estimation During Speech
papers.summary: Event cameras offer high temporal resolution and low power consumption, making them promising for speech-related applications. These include automatic lip reading, audiovisual speech analysis, and human-robot interaction, particularly in challenging environments characterized by low illumination or high dynamic range. Event-based lip reading, speaker recognition, and voice activity detection, however, mostly operate on a cropped region of interest (ROI), by hand or by the dataset, and no event-based method supplies that ROI as a spatial region; existing event-based face analysis gives the mouth as landmarks, which presents a mismatch between application and localization. The present work predicts a dense heatmap over the lip region from the full event "frame". Events are encoded as a polarity-separated voxel grid and processed at every location by a two-pathway continuous-time recurrent network (CT-RNN) with learned, log-space bounded time constants acting on the real elapsed time of each bin: a stateless fast pathway and a stateful slow pathway, utilised for refining and anchoring the prediction. The model reaches 69.5% on lips on four unseen speakers and switches target only 2.1 times per second, against 8.9 and 11.0 for convolutional baselines with more parameters. Adding a spatial encoder improves precision but fails on a new face scale. On a real event sensor, trained only on simulated events, the proposed model reaches 58.0% on lips against 43.2% for the CNN, with fewer than half its target switches.

papers.title: Convergence of the quasinormal-mode expansion of the Kerr Green function
papers.summary: Black-hole ringdown is usually modeled as a linear superposition of quasinormal modes, and fits to gravitational-wave observations increasingly include high overtones. However, the overtone sum does not necessarily converge: overtones are more strongly damped and thus decay faster in time, but their amplitudes in the Green function (the signal at an observer produced by an impulse at a source point) grow, so the mode description may break down before a finite time. We show that for a rotating (Kerr) black hole this time has a clear geometric meaning. For highly damped modes, the amplitudes grow exponentially with the optical distance from the source and the observer to a characteristic "bounce" radius close to the black hole, defined as the location where the mode amplitude is smallest. For one family of modes, the amplitudes are also suppressed the farther the source and observer sit from the equatorial plane. Rotation therefore makes the onset of convergence depend on direction as well as distance, extending the geometric picture from bounce radii to bounce surfaces. Combining these effects gives a sufficient condition for absolute convergence. For spin $a/M = 0.7$, we map how this time varies with source and observer position, and amplitudes computed numerically reproduce the predicted spatial dependence to better than one percent. These results set geometric limits on when the quasinormal-mode sums converge.

papers.title: FMT: Lossless Image Compression in a Fixed Number of Parallel Steps
papers.summary: Learned lossless codecs make smaller files than common classical codecs, yet the images we archive and train on still use classical codecs. A main reason is time: a learned codec takes seconds to decode a photo that a classical codec opens in milliseconds, and their faster variants give up most of their gain in size. We argue that much of this time is spent waiting, not computing: the network waits for the values it conditions on, and the arithmetic decoder reads them one at a time. We introduce FMT (Fixed-step Multiscale Tree), a lossless image format whose decoding order and entropy coder are designed together so that neither wait grows with the image. FMT stores an image as a coarse-to-fine tree whose steps hold independent values: a GPU predicts each step at once and decodes it in parallel rANS lanes that carry their states from step to step, so an image of any size decodes in a fixed number of sequential steps. On this tree we build a family of bit-exact codecs, from a rule with no network to large networks, and no codec we ran on the same GPU beats any of them on both size and speed. Without a network, FMT beats NVIDIA's HTJ2K on size and speed; with a large one, it decodes Kodak photos 9 to 61X faster than learned codecs we ran on the same A100, at the same size or smaller.

papers.title: Riemannian geometry and quantum gravity on trees
papers.summary: We show that the tree graphs that admit a quantum Riemannian geometry (QRG) with a positive ratio metric are exactly the Dynkin graphs of finite type $A,D,E$ and affine type $\widetilde D,\widetilde E$. A metric in this context is an assignment of a nonzero real value to each arrow and positive ratio requires that the two directions on any edge have the same sign. It turns out that the metric value in one direction can be chosen freely and the other is then determined. For finite $A, D, E$ type, the construction involves $q$-integers where $q=e^{\imathπ/h}$ with $h$ the Coxeter number and there is a conjugate pair of $*$-preserving quantum Levi-Civita connections (QLCs). In the case of type $A$, these are necessarily contained in a previously known 1-parameter space of connections. For affine $\widetilde D,\widetilde E$ type, there is only one QLC, with real coefficients. Using the quantum Riemannian geometry, we construct a natural Einstein--Hilbert action and hence new quantum gravity models on $A_3,D_4,\widetilde D_4,\widetilde D_5,\widetilde D_6,\widetilde E_6$ in a functional integral approach, other than the 4-star $\widetilde D_4$ which we revisit.

papers.title: CADENCE: Learning Acyclic Gaits for Model-Based Quadruped Locomotion
papers.summary: Model-based quadruped controllers usually step on a cyclic gait, which lifts the legs in a fixed order on a fixed period, wherever the safe footholds are. We present CADENCE, a learned step planner with a small action space. Every 40 ms, it picks one of at most 65 discrete choices: no step, or one leg's step to a safe foothold. It also predicts a swing time. We train CADENCE by reinforcement learning on top of a convex model predictive controller (MPC). Nothing prescribes a gait: there is no gait schedule, and the reward has no gait term, only a cost per step. The one structural constraint is that at most two legs may swing at once. The policy we analyzed developed an acyclic gait, with no fixed period or stepping order, yet it still paired diagonal legs. An inverse footstep model (IFM), fitted on a controller's logged steps, turns each foothold into a command. With only the IFM refitted, on fewer than 20,000 steps, CADENCE ran frozen on OCS2's nonlinear MPC. In simulated trials on a range of terrains (26% to 49% voids) and speeds (0.1 m/s and 0.2 m/s), it succeeded in 85.1% (mean of five seeds), against 67.8% for OCS2-Trot, 65.5% for OCS2-Single, and 39.6% in a static walk ablation of CADENCE. At 49% voids, it succeeded in 72.9%, against 43.0% for OCS2-Trot.

papers.title: Inference for Heterogeneous Treatment Effects with Deep Survival Learners
papers.summary: Conditional average treatment effects (CATEs) provide a principled framework for assessing treatment-effect heterogeneity and identifying patients who may benefit from an intervention. For survival outcomes, CATEs may also evolve over time and pose challenges for estimation and inference. Existing methods can accommodate complex covariate heterogeneity but often fail to exploit shared temporal structure or provide valid inference for time-varying treatment effects and their contrasts. We propose a deep survival learning framework that combines neural networks for nonparametric covariate effects with a shared spline representation of temporal variation, enabling joint estimation of CATE trajectories. Using doubly robust pseudo-outcomes and sample splitting, we establish nonasymptotic oracle bounds accounting for network and temporal approximation, nuisance estimation, and optimization errors. Our theory shows that exploiting shared temporal structure yields sharper error bounds for temporal contrasts than those derived from separate time-specific estimators. For inference, we develop a subsampled ensemble procedure and establish asymptotic normality for pointwise CATEs, temporal contrasts, and covariate contrasts, including temporal contrasts over shrinking time intervals. Under suitable regularity and bias-control conditions, consistent infinitesimal jackknife variance estimators yield asymptotically valid confidence intervals. Simulations evaluate estimation accuracy, interval coverage, and sensitivity to temporal dimension and basis mismatch. An application to lung cancer survival data illustrates the framework's ability to characterize heterogeneous treatment benefits over time.

papers.title: Event-Based Person Detection for Maritime UAV Search
papers.summary: Maritime search and rescue requires locating people in the water quickly, motivating the use of UAVs to survey the search area. During flight, camera motion and the longer exposures used in low light can blur small targets and hinder person detection. Event cameras record brightness changes as they occur, reducing the motion blur associated with longer exposure times. We investigate their use for maritime person detection by generating synthetic events using the v2e event simulator from public MOBDrone rescue videos and retaining the existing annotations. We compare the recurrent vision transformer model RVT-T with YOLOv8n and RT-DETR-R18 trained on exposure-matched images. On 843 test samples from held-out recordings, RVT-T achieves 15.63% person AP50:95, compared with 6.89% for YOLOv8n and 9.44% for RT-DETR-R18 under 100 ms synthetic exposure. Increasing exposure times from 50 to 200 ms progressively reduces frame-based detection accuracy, widening the gap to the event model. To evaluate the feasibility of on-board processing, we deploy our detector on a Jetson Orin Nano platform. The RVT-T model retains its accuracy and requires approximately 136 ms and 2.02 J per sample, allowing real-time processing on the UAV.
papers.comment: Accepted at the 5th Workshop on Maritime Computer Vision (MaCVi), WACV 2027

papers.title: Transfer Once, Ask Locally: Compact Audio-Visual Memory for On-Device Question Answering
papers.summary: Audio-visual question answering on lightweight user devices requires balancing speed, memory usage, privacy, and communication. One approach is to run audio-visual encoders on a server and a lightweight language decoder on the user device, keeping questions local while offloading media encoding. However, transferring and processing the full multimodal representation remains costly. We propose a training-free, query-agnostic token pruning framework that constructs a compact, reusable memory before transmission. We define video spatio-temporal blocks and aligned audio windows as players and estimate their importance through Monte Carlo Shapley valuation. We use an embedding coverage objective that combines query-independent utility with cross-modal redundancy calibration and rewards unimodal diversity through marginal coverage gains. We retain the original token embeddings of high-scoring players under a limited token budget and transfer the resulting memory once for reuse across subsequent local questions. Experiments on Video-MME, Daily-Omni, and Video-Holmes using video-SALMONN 2+ (3B) and video-SALMONN 2 Pro (4B) show that our method achieves the best or tied-best QA accuracy among the compared compression methods across all evaluated settings. On Daily-Omni with video-SALMONN 2+ (3B) at 80\% pruning, our method improves accuracy by 12.86--14.62 percentage points over these methods while achieving the lowest device-side LLM prefill and decoding latency, with up to $1.92\times$ decoding speedup at comparable embedding memory usage.

papers.title: An Efficient Method for Directly Integrating the Vlasov Equation in Collisionless and Weakly-Collisional Simulations
papers.summary: We describe and test a new numerical method to solve the Vlasov/Boltzmann equation in systems with arbitrary levels of collisionality. The method combines recent ideas to evolve the distribution function (DF) directly in 6+1 dimensional phase-space in a manner which is Lagrangian in both position+velocity. The 'particles' of traditional Monte-Carlo/Particle-In-Cell/N-body (MC/PIC/NB) methods become mesh-generating points defining a volume partition, each of which carries a set of momentum-Lagrangian basis functions representing a local anisotropic momentum DF. The DF is then integrated between cells and bases via a higher-order reconstruction and Godunov-type method, evolving a 10 or 13-moment representation of each basis to ensure manifest mass/momentum/energy conservation. The method allows one to represent arbitrary DFs, including multiple independent streams but also collisional or phase-mixed or thermal distributions (unlike traditional 'moments' or waterbag/tessellation methods), and the cost is bounded to a modest multiplier of MC/PIC/NB costs. We provide an example implementation which uses a spatially-Lagrangian volume partition, second-order reconstruction, and simple set of bases which ensure constant cell masses and couple directly to existing MC/PIC/NB machinery, made public in the code GIZMO. We validate in a series of test problems, demonstrating manifest conservation, Galilean and translation and rotation invariance, and ability to represent complex DFs without spurious dissipation or instability. We discuss applications where this method can have advantages compared to traditional algorithms for simulations of dark matter, stellar, weakly-collisional neutral gas, and particulate/dust dynamics; multiphase/polydisperse flows; cosmic ray and radiation transport/hydrodynamics; and plasma physics.
papers.comment: 31 pages, 20 figures, submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics. Comments welcome. Implementation in the public GIZMO code available at http://www.tapir.caltech.edu/~phopkins/Site/GIZMO.html

papers.title: Probing Lorentz-violating electrodynamics with CMB polarization. II. Updated constraints and forecasts for the Simons Observatory and LiteBIRD
papers.summary: We update the constraints on Lorentz-violating electrodynamics from the polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Within the minimal Standard Model Extension, we consider the renormalizable CPT-odd and CPT-even operators of the photon sector, which source cosmic birefringence and circular polarization, respectively. Combining Planck, Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and South Pole Telescope (SPT) temperature and $E$-mode data with $B$-mode measurements from BICEP/Keck, SPT-3G D1 and SPTpol, we constrain the CPT-odd coefficients to $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|<7.75\times10^{-45}$ GeV and $|\mathbf{k_{AF}}|<3.82\times10^{-45}$ GeV at 95% credible level. These are the strongest bounds to date from any probe, and are driven by the SPT-3G D1 $B$-mode data. For the first time in this type of analysis, we also include the Planck PR4 $EB$ spectrum, which yields a mild preference for a non-zero $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|$. For the CPT-even coefficient, we find $k_{F,E+B}<5.99\times10^{-32}$. Including the latest circular polarization measurements from the Cosmology Large Angular Scale Surveyor (CLASS) tightens this bound by about 7%. This is the first time that CMB circular polarization data contribute to constraining this coefficient. Finally, we forecast the sensitivity of the Simons Observatory (SO) and LiteBIRD. With linear polarization only, the two experiments are complementary, with SO tightening the CPT-even bound by about 30% and LiteBIRD the CPT-odd ones by 40 to 45%. Exploiting the sensitivity to circular polarization provided by the non-idealities of its half-wave plate, LiteBIRD could also improve the CPT-even bound by more than an order of magnitude.

papers.title: A Unified Choice Model of News Selection: Experimental Evidence on Stance, Rank, and Engagement Cues
papers.summary: Social media platforms often display visual engagement cues alongside ranked news articles, yet their influence on clicks remains poorly understood when considered jointly with ranking position and users' political preferences. We propose a unified discrete choice framework using a conditional multinomial logit model to jointly estimate and compare the influence of these factors on news selection. We evaluate the model using 1,480 choices from 370 human participants across four news topics in a controlled study with and without visual engagement cues. The framework allows us to assess the incremental contribution of each factor through nested-model likelihood-ratio tests. We find that including visual engagement cues significantly improves model fit across all topics after accounting for rank and stance. Engagement cues alone also predict clicks better than either of these features, although the full model achieves the highest held-out log-likelihood. Finally, we quantify via counterfactual analysis the impact of ranking position and displayed engagement counts on click probabilities. These findings can inform platform owners, researchers, and policymakers evaluating how platform design affects the selection of political news.

papers.title: UnrealEvent: Synthetic Dataset Generation and Annotation for Event-Based Vision
papers.summary: Event-based cameras provide high temporal resolution, low power consumption, and a high dynamic range, but progress in event-based object detection remains constrained by the scarcity of annotated training data. To solve this issue, this paper introduces the tool UnrealEvent, a synthetic dataset-generation pipeline implemented in Unreal Engine 5.5. The pipeline combines a V2E-inspired event-frame generator with EasySynth semantic-rendering passes, allowing rendered level sequences to be converted into paired event representations and YOLO-format bounding-box annotations without manual labeling. Events are generated from per-pixel log-luminance differences between consecutive frames, with contrast thresholds sampled independently from a normal distribution to emulate the fabrication-induced threshold mismatch of real sensors. Using this pipeline, we provide a synthetic dataset and evaluate YOLOv8 detectors under synthetic, zero-shot real, and real fine-tuning training on eTraM. The results show strong in-domain synthetic performance but a substantial synthetic-to-real gap, especially for pedestrians. Fine-tuning on a small real subset improves real-domain performance, while the remaining gap highlights the importance of asset diversity and sensor calibration.
papers.comment: Accepted at the Workshop on Neuromorphic Vision (NeVi), ECCV 2026

papers.title: Flavor-dependent quark-mass scaling and the fate of the strange-matter window in self-bound quark stars
papers.summary: In the flavor-dependent QMDD model, self-bound $ud$ quark matter can be the ground state at vanishing pressure and convert into $uds$ matter through a first-order transition. So far the mass functional has used parameters $(a,C)$ common to all flavors; here we let the strange sector have its own coupling, $C_s=α\,C_{u,d}$, and map the response of the zero-pressure parameter space. The $e^0_{ud}=930\,$MeV boundary is independent of $α$ by construction, whereas increasing $α$ enlarges the self-bound $ud$ domain and pushes the $e^0_{ud}=e^0_{uds}$ line towards larger $a$. The causality boundary $c^0_s=c$ is almost frozen near $a\simeq5.5$. The competition closes the strange-matter window at \RA{$α_{\rm crit}\simeq1.136$}: above it every causal self-bound parametrization is $ud$ at zero pressure, so a first-order $ud\!\to\!uds$ transition must occur at higher pressure, though not necessarily inside a star, since the maximum mass may be reached below the transition density. The transition pressure and the energy-density jump grow monotonically with $α$, both scale \RB{approximately} with the available-volume fraction $q=1-κ$, and the Seidov onset-instability diagnostic stays below unity.

papers.title: PAIR: Bringing Household Robots into the Smart Home
papers.summary: Household robots often need to operate appliances, and smart appliances offer both control panels and device APIs. Existing embodied AI simulation environments, however, model appliances solely as physical objects. We introduce PAIR, a smart-home simulation environment grounded in the Matter protocol~\footnote{https://csa-iot.org/all-solutions/matter/}, the industry standard for smart-home devices. PAIR provides 84 smart-device assets whose functional control panels and APIs act on a shared device state, with ambient conditions that evolve in response to both. From a survey of 1,443 requests, we construct a benchmark of 40 tasks that all require object manipulation yet remain solvable without API access, with 340 human demonstrations for policy training. Whether run alone, with a high-level planner, or with an API-enabled planner, two fine-tuned VLA policies complete none of the 120 evaluation episodes. Robots rarely get far enough to use the API: even with oracle plans and API access, over 90\% of failed rollouts stall at navigating, grasping, or operating a door. With a perfect oracle in place of the robot's body, the best planner still gets through only 57.3\% of its plan. When choosing between pressing a button and calling an API, several planners go by whether they can read the panel, not by API latency.\footnote{We will release our code and data upon publication.}

papers.title: Integrating market sentiments for stock price prediction: A comparative study of Bi-LSTM and multilayer perceptions
papers.summary: This study investigates the integration of sentiment analysis with machine learning models to forecast stock price movements using the Nvidia Corporation as a case study. Sentiment scores were derived from Nvidia-related financial news headlines using two sentiment analysis tools: FinBERT, a domain-specific tool, and TextBlob, a general-purpose tool. These scores were integrated into predictive frameworks based on bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) networks and multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) developed alongside historical stock price data. This study assesses the predictive performance over the entire observation period and across distinct market phases: bullish, stagnation, and strong bullish conditions. The findings indicate that sentiment features enhance predictive accuracy in specific contexts, particularly during stagnation phases, with TextBlob demonstrating superior performance to FinBERT in specific scenarios. In addition, Bi-LSTM models exhibit consistently superior performance in capturing temporal dependencies compared to MLPs. However, the impact of sentiment features diminished during strongly directional trends, such as those observed in strong bullish markets. The combination of FinBERT and TextBlob in the same dataset allows for a dual-perspective approach to sentiment analysis, thereby providing new insights into the dynamic relationship between market sentiment and stock price behavior. This research contributes to the existing literature on applying sentiment analysis to financial forecasting by advancing the integration of complementary sentiment tools and phase-specific evaluations.
papers.comment: 23 pages. Published in Istanbul Business Research, 54(1), 99-121 (2025), under the CC BY-NC 4.0 license. DOI: 10.26650/ibr.2025.54.1470756

papers.title: RFW-S: Everyday Deformable Objects with Independent Simulation Verification
papers.summary: Large-scale robotic simulation requires diverse deformable objects with executable physical properties and realistic interaction behaviors. However, existing 3D asset collections primarily emphasize visual diversity, while scalable physical construction and verification remain challenging. We introduce RFW-S, a large-scale dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified assets spanning 485 everyday categories across five structural families: soft solids, cloth sheets, shells, garments, and bags. We develop an automated pipeline integrating reference-guided 3D generation, structure-aware physical modeling, and LLM-assisted parameter estimation and calibration. To ensure physical reliability, we introduce an independent simulation verification framework that evaluates object behaviors under interactions distinct from those used for parameter calibration. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of independent verification and characterize deformable responses under different physical configurations. We further evaluate robotic grasping in terms of both task success and object integrity, and demonstrate the physical realism of our simulated objects through sim-to-real replay of fragile-object manipulation. RFW-S provides a scalable foundation for physically grounded simulation and embodied robotic learning.

papers.title: FrameRouter: Frame Budget Routing for Long-Video Understanding on Video-MME-v2 and Beyond
papers.summary: Long-video question answering benchmarks like Video-MME-v2 typically evaluate systems under a uniform frame budget for every question, despite stark variation in the evidence each query actually demands. We analyze this mismatch on Video-MME-v2 and find that different question subsets prefer different frozen frame-budget policies, while uniformly increasing the frame count does not reliably improve all metrics. These findings motivate fixed-mean frame-budget routing, a controlled inference setting in which each question may receive a different frame budget while the average budget matches a uniform reference. We introduce FrameRouter, a training-free test-time framework that combines an evidence-demand router, a budget-constrained allocation rule, and a frozen bank of frame-sampling policies. By controlling how much visual evidence each question receives while leaving the underlying samplers unchanged, FrameRouter is orthogonal to query-aware frame selection. Across Video-MME-v2 and several long-video understanding benchmarks, FrameRouter improves long-video question answering by using the same average visual budget more selectively across questions. Code is available at https://github.com/bingjunluo/FrameRouter.

papers.title: ReTouchGS: Ultralight Render-free Aesthetic Color Enhancement and Transfer for 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables photorealistic scene reconstruction. Existing 3DGS color transfer and interactive editing methods are guided by reference images and user-specified color adjustments. However, in many applications, users simply want aesthetically guided color enhancement that automatically makes the scene more visually appealing while maintaining consistent colors and tones across viewpoints. We present ReTouchGS, to our knowledge the first framework for reference-free aesthetic color enhancement of pretrained 3DGS models. It predicts a scene-level color lookup table (LUT) from the model and its associated camera parameters. ReTouchGS also supports reference-guided color transfer by fitting a scene-level LUT using one edited view of the same scene and its corresponding original render. A shared blend-aware color refinement network with only 44.7K parameters refines an analytic color update to realize either color mapping without rendering. It preserves geometry and delivers standard 3DGS assets in seconds. We also design the ReTouch3D benchmark to support the evaluation of aesthetic color enhancement and reference-guided color transfer across viewpoints. Experiments demonstrate high color accuracy and strong generalization to unseen scenes in both aesthetic color enhancement and reference-guided color transfer.

papers.title: Refin3R: Geometry-Guided Refinement for Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction
papers.summary: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models predict dense point maps from multiple images in a single pass. Without explicit geometric constraints, however, their predictions are often inconsistent across views and lack fine-grained precision. Recent methods incorporate geometric priors such as camera pose or depth, but use them merely as auxiliary inputs, process each view independently, or refine the geometry only where the priors are available. We present Refin3R, which refines feed-forward point maps with Structure-from-Motion (SfM) points, propagating SfM geometry over the image grid. In its dual-branch architecture, a 2D branch extends SfM geometry beyond its coverage using geometry-aware backbone features, while a 3D branch reasons over the SfM points of all views, capturing multi-view structure that the image grid alone cannot represent. The two branches exchange information bidirectionally to jointly refine each view, yielding dense and accurate point maps. Across ScanNet++, ETH3D, Tanks\&Temples, and out-of-domain human and surgical scenes, Refin3R consistently outperforms feed-forward and geometry-guided methods in point map accuracy while running faster than the strongest geometry-guided baseline.

papers.title: Magflow: Differentiable Simulation of Industrial-Grade 6D Magnetic Levitation
papers.summary: Magnetic levitation with six-degrees-of-freedom enables frictionless transport and micrometer-scale positioning in principle, but low-level control is inherently challenging due to its complex and unstable dynamics. Industrial systems typically rely on deep hardware-software co-design, where mover and stator geometries are jointly designed to enable a compact, hand-crafted approximation of the electromagnetic force computation, thereby keeping control computationally tractable at kilohertz rates. However, this approach imposes overly conservative constraints on the operating workspace and the range of supported mover topologies. Instead of reducing the underlying physics to a hand-crafted approximation, we compute the physics directly. We introduce Magflow, a fully differentiable, GPU-parallel simulator for 6D magnetic levitation. It is used to train the first neural controller for an industrial-grade 6D magnetic levitation system that is learned purely from simulated physics. We show that the learned neural controller transfers zero-shot from simulation to real hardware while satisfying hard real-time constraints at 4 kHz. The learned controller achieves qualitatively new behaviors and even levitates a mover topology for which no hand-crafted solution exists. These results demonstrate that co-design is not a physical necessity for 6D magnetic levitation control. More broadly, control learning from simulated physics can find solutions beyond the reach of control engineering in demanding industrial domains. Source code and demonstration videos are publicly available at https://sites.google.com/view/magflow.
papers.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L). Project page: https://sites.google.com/view/magflow

papers.title: Wall-to-wall maps of canopy height and aboveground carbon across the Atlantic Forest
papers.summary: Global canopy height maps are increasingly used to estimate forest carbon, yet their regional accuracy is rarely tested. We present wall-to-wall maps of canopy height (10~m) and aboveground carbon density (30~m) for the Brazilian Atlantic Forest in 2024. Height was predicted by a deep learning network fusing Sentinel-2 reflectance, Sentinel-1 and ALOS PALSAR backscatter and ALOS elevation, trained on 7{,}179 and tested on 1{,}793 patches (58{,}800~km$^2$) from a statewide airborne LiDAR campaign over São Paulo state, Brazil. On held-out test patches, the root mean square error is 3.05~m at 10~m and 2.58~m at 30~m, and the model was validated at two LiDAR sites outside São Paulo. Over the same pixels, the Meta and World Resources Institute global product has more than twice this error. A power law fitted to 124 inventory plots converted canopy height to above ground carbon density. The remaining forest holds 1{,}944~Tg~C over 28.3~Mha. Global products therefore need local validation before use in carbon accounting.
papers.comment: 56 pages, 13 figures, 8 tables, 2 supplementary tables. Submitted to Scientific Data. Maps and code openly available via Zenodo and GitHub

papers.title: Frequency Multiplexing of Purcell-Enhanced Optically Coherent NV Centers
papers.summary: Integrating optically coherent quantum emitters into nanophotonic structures is key to scalable quantum networks. Realizing them with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is hindered by the degradation of optical coherence accompanying nanofabrication. Here, we overcome this challenge by integrating multiple NV centers into a monolithic diamond photonic crystal nanocavity while preserving near-lifetime-limited optical coherence. We observe linewidths as narrow as 19 MHz, enabling the frequency multiplexing of spectrally distinct NV centers within a common cavity mode, while maintaining charge-state stability over several minutes under resonant excitation. Tuning the cavity into resonance with the NV zero-phonon line enhances the optical emission, consistent with Purcell enhancement predicted by finite-element simulations. Additionally, individual cavities can be independently brought into resonance with NV zero-phonon lines on the same chip. These results combine bulk-like optical coherence with frequency multiplexing and cavity-enhanced emission, establishing a scalable nanophotonic platform for NV-based quantum network nodes.

papers.title: Precision Muon Physics
papers.summary: The muon has become a versatile tool for fundamental physics. Measurements of muon decay determine the Fermi constant and establish the chiral structure of weak interactions. Measurements with stored muons and bound muons enable precision determinations of the muon charge, mass, and magnetic moment. These studies also provide far-reaching tests of bound-state QED and the Standard Model, as well as unique sensitivity to physics beyond our current understanding of the particles, forces, and laws of nature. We survey the landscape of precision muon physics, emphasizing both the physics reach and the experimental breadth. We highlight the range of techniques, from charged-particle timing, tracking, and polarimetry to storage-ring experiments, microwave resonance methods, and Doppler-free laser spectroscopy. We also describe the interplay between experimental work and theoretical developments in quantum electrodynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and effective field theory.
papers.comment: 30 pages, 11 figures, contribution prepared for Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics by Elsevier

papers.title: Right shape, wrong time: phase errors of ODE solvers in the flame problem
papers.summary: The flame model $y'=y^2-y^3$, $y(0)=δ$, is a standard illustration of stiffness: for $δ=10^{-4}$ the stiff MATLAB solvers ode23s and ode15s need only 99 and 140 steps, against 3040 for ode45. We show that these cheap solutions have the right shape at the wrong time: they place the front 29 and 329 time units early, with maximal errors 0.95 and 1.00. Because all solutions are time translates of one master profile, the global error of every numerical solution with values in $[δ,1)$ is exactly a phase error, $y_k=y_δ(t_k-D_k)$. For fixed-step one-step methods of order $p$ we prove $D=h^p\int_δ^{y}g+O(h^{p+1})$ with a remainder bounded uniformly in $δ$, so that the delay grows at most like $h\ln(1/δ)$ for $p=1$ and stays bounded for $p\geq2$. For any computed solution the delay is exactly the sum of its defects with respect to the exact flow, converted into time; a heuristic model, confirmed by MATLAB runs, explains why it is created in the first few steps and why tightening the tolerances is an expensive cure. Integrating for $1/y$, which runs like a clock in the slow phase, with an absolute tolerance reduces the error by several orders of magnitude, at a median cost close to that of the standard formulation. The mechanism needs only that the equation is autonomous; its general form is the subject of a companion paper.
papers.comment: 28 pages, 10 figures, 9 tables; supplementary Tables S1-S6 in the ancillary file. Code and data: https://github.com/boros91/flame-phase-errors (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24314322)

papers.title: Dissecting the GPU Load/Store Unit and Exposing Its Security Risks
papers.summary: GPUs are the main platform for large-scale machine learning and power the largest supercomputers. Their load/store units (LSUs) often determine kernel performance and have been exploited in prior attacks. Yet what is known about the LSU is only a few isolated mechanisms and parameters, and even a single one has been enough for an attack. In particular, it is still unknown what a load costs, where loads contend, and even whether a warp can starve due to contention. Until each is measured, neither its security risk nor a defense is known. We reverse-engineer how the LSU serves load instructions on recent NVIDIA GPUs with microbenchmarks and analyze the security implications. We give a cycle-accurate latency formula for a global L1 hit or shared memory access from the addresses it touches, whose address-dependent terms are bank conflicts and the L1 tag lookup; we show that loads contend at both, and that when the LSU pipeline is full a warp can starve a warp of a later-launched block. We then show that the LSU's attack surface is far broader than prior attacks revealed: through channels never exploited before, it can leak information, communicate covertly, and degrade colocated workloads. Through either global bank conflicts or tag lookups alone, we recover a full AES-128 key under the threat model of prior GPU AES timing attacks. Under NVIDIA's Multi-Process Service (MPS), the bank access and the tag lookup each open a covert channel across processes, whose rate rises with each GPU generation. Also under MPS, this starvation lets one warp slow a colocated cuBLAS matrix multiplication by up to 750x on the A100 and 563x on the H100.

papers.title: Satisfiability Modulo Theories for Robust Synthesis of Signal Temporal Logic Specifications
papers.summary: Signal Temporal Logic is a popular framework for describing a robotic system's goals. Once described using a temporal logic framework, synthesis turns the goals into actual steps for the robots to follow. Currently, the state of the art for sound and complete synthesis is using Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP), which struggles on long time horizons and large environments, preventing the construction of guaranteed safe plans for long deployments. This paper introduces a new synthesis method using Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) which scales better for long deployments and adapts to environmental changes more quickly. We do this by introducing an encoding method for STL into SMT constraints, and an encoding method for discrete-time dynamical systems modeled as a transition system. We then conduct an empirical comparison of our SMT based methods against the state of the art MILP based methods. Results show that for this class of problems, SMT is an effective encoding strategy that performs the best on long time horizon tasks.

papers.title: Variable-length MDI QKD under source imperfections and local randomization over horizontal links
papers.summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) provides security guarantees that hold despite device imperfections and finite-size effects. We address these challenges in measurement-device-independent (MDI) QKD, combining its intrinsic untrusted detection with an imperfection model for Alice's and Bob's sources via fidelity bounds. We establish variable-length general security under the Marginal-constrained Entropy Accumulation Theorem (MEAT), estimating the relevant Rényi entropies through conic optimization. We evaluate our model under a horizontal channel link, reporting secret keys for blocks as small as n~3x10^4 rounds under atmosphere-free conditions, and show that compensating for unequal channel attenuation through appropriately chosen transmitted amplitudes improves performance in asymmetric configurations, enabling communication distances beyond 80 km for commercial satellite systems.

papers.title: \texttt{StochAXtic}: a JAX-Accelerated, End-to-End Differentiable Framework for Gravitational-Wave Backgrounds from Compact Binary Populations
papers.summary: We present \texttt{StochAXtic}, a package for computing the dimensionless energy density spectrum $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ of the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by compact binary coalescences. Rather than sampling binary populations via Monte Carlo, \texttt{StochAXtic} exploits the \emph{scale invariance} of the waveforms: at fixed mass ratio, spins and tidal deformabilities, the waveform depends on the total mass only through the dimensionless combination $Mf$. This allows all computationally expensive waveform evaluations using \texttt{LALSuite} to be performed once and stored in a population-independent lookup table. The subsequent integrals over mass and redshift can then be recast as convolutions and evaluated efficiently using fast Fourier transforms. We further employ truncated singular value decomposition to compress the lookup table, reducing both computational cost and memory requirements. Once the table has been computed and cached, \texttt{StochAXtic} evaluates $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ in a few milliseconds, achieving a relative numerical error below $10^{-3}$ at frequencies up to $1$ kHz. Its results agree with those of \texttt{popstock} within the latter's statistical uncertainties. Implemented entirely in \texttt{JAX}, \texttt{StochAXtic} also provides gradients of $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ with respect to population hyperparameters, enabling its direct integration with gradient-based inference methods including Hamiltonian Monte Carlo.

papers.title: Residual-Guided Lightweight Reinforcement Learning for Risk-Aware Trajectory Selection with a Frozen World Model
papers.summary: In automated driving, world models provide future scene predictions for evaluating candidate trajectories, but fixed selection rules may not capture scene-dependent trade-offs. We propose a residual-guided reinforcement learning (RL) framework for lightweight trajectory selection with a frozen world model and a fixed candidate bank. The framework uses proximal policy optimization (PPO) to fine-tune a joint policy over candidate selection and bounded trajectory residuals. A context-conditioned ranking network learns candidate preferences from feedback obtained by evaluating local perturbations of the selected trajectories. At inference, the selector combines learned preference and predicted risk ranks using fixed weights and returns the selected candidate trajectory without modification. Fine-tuning updates 16,106 parameters across the actor and critic, while the deployed selector retains only the 11,725-parameter ranking network, with the residual branch and critic used exclusively during training. In open-loop evaluation on the nuScenes validation set, the method reduces average Euclidean trajectory error (L2) by 3.99% relative to the RiskWorld model baseline without RL-based selection. Under matched budgets for feedback accesses and actor updates, residual exploration reduces L2 by 0.83% relative to the categorical PPO variant trained without residuals. The method also maintains lower L2 than RiskWorld when risk features are removed or shuffled.

papers.title: Making Future-Predictive Representations Actionable
papers.summary: Recent world action models (WAMs) drop future prediction at inference, assuming that representations learned through auxiliary future supervision still benefit action generation. However, our layerwise analysis of Fast-WAM reveals a depth-dependent mismatch: while probes decode future state transitions more accurately from deeper visual layers, the gradients and visual focuses of the future and action objectives increasingly diverge with depth, leaving much of this predictive information unused by the action pathway. To address this issue, we introduce RelayWAM, which adds an explicit transition space between the video and action backbones. Conditioned on the task instruction, robot state, and current action estimate, recurrent transition layers extract step-relevant predictive cues across depth and relay them directly into the action attention, without generating future frames at inference. Experiments show that RelayWAM substantially amplifies the benefit of future supervision, translating into stronger generalization under distribution shifts in both simulation and real-world robot tasks. On LIBERO-Plus, RelayWAM achieves 72.03% mean success, compared to 56.42% without future supervision and 51.50% for Fast-WAM.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 6 main figures, including supplementary material

papers.title: Physics-Informed Tactile-based Shape Estimation of Deformable Linear Objects
papers.summary: Accurate shape estimation of Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs) is a fundamental challenge in robotic manipulation, often hindered by visual occlusions and the high-dimensional configuration space of flexible materials. While Force/Torque (F/T) and vision-centric methods have been proposed, they frequently struggle with grasp-site ambiguities and environmental interference. In this letter, we investigate the hypothesis that global shape estimation can be achieved through tactile sensing and proprioception, without any visual perception. We contend that dense, high-resolution tactile imprints capture critical boundary conditions and contact gradients that are sufficient to resolve the high-dimensional configuration of the DLO. To prove this, we introduce a Physics-Informed Vision Transformer (ViT) framework that maps tactile images to a 3D vertex chain. By leveraging self-attention mechanisms and a physics-weighted loss function, our model enforces structural priors to ensure that the predicted geometry adheres to the object's physical manifold. Experimental results demonstrate that our tactile-based approach achieves superior reconstruction accuracy across Euclidean and Chamfer metrics. Furthermore, we demonstrate the efficiency of this modality, achieving model transfer to novel DLO materials and geometries. Our findings suggest that tactile feedback provides a robust and computationally efficient alternative for DLO state estimation in visually degraded or occluded environments.

papers.title: How Web Research Agents Interpret User Priorities
papers.summary: Web research agents gather information online and write cited reports, including financial analysis. Users can state a priority to guide this research, but a priority may not say how to judge the options, leaving the agent to choose the criteria. We examine how two such agents, built on OpenAI and Anthropic models, interpret a stated priority. In 36 runs, the agents compared Microsoft and Alphabet as businesses. Prompts asked for special attention to growth or resilience, or gave no priority. We analyzed reports, searches, returned sources and cited sources. Of the 24 reports given a priority, 21 focused on it, but their criteria varied. Under the growth priority, OpenAI reports that ranked the companies accounted for risk or predictability and favored Microsoft, while the Anthropic ones judged growth by its pace and favored Alphabet. Under the resilience priority, reports used partly different criteria, and most named Microsoft as the more resilient company. Of the search and source measures tested, only the Anthropic agent's search wording differed detectably by condition. These findings suggest evaluations should examine the criteria behind a report's judgements, not only its focus or accuracy. Interfaces could let users see and adjust those criteria.

papers.title: Structured AI ideation yields physical strategies for epithelial barrier repair
papers.summary: AI systems increasingly support literature analysis, candidate evaluation and hypothesis refinement, but enabling researchers to explore research directions beyond established disciplinary approaches remains challenging. We developed Abelio, an AI system designed to generate novel research directions by expanding investigators' avenues of inquiry. Abelio reformulates research objectives, uses these alternative formulations to identify relevant elements outside conventional disciplinary boundaries, and refines the resulting hypotheses. Each stage integrates divergent exploration with convergent selection through a dedicated subsystem. In quantitative evaluations, proposals generated by the Ideation Core (Abelio's hypothesis-generation core) outperformed those of four frontier large language models in scientific soundness and hypothesis diversity, and three of four in distance from existing literature. Subsystem ablation showed that each subsystem contributes to the property it targets, with the contribution of Element Selection measurable before Refinement. To investigate intestinal epithelial barrier restoration, Abelio proposed physical interventions involving membrane-tethered poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) and cholesterol-anchored complementary DNA. Both proposals were archived before experimentation and subsequently tested independently in damaged Caco-2 monolayers. PEG preserved barrier function in a membrane-surface-dependent manner, whereas complementary DNA enabled sequence-specific restoration that was reversible on demand. These findings demonstrate how structured research ideation can identify experimentally testable approaches beyond established disciplinary conventions.

papers.title: Strangeness-to-entropy ratio across the QCD crossover
papers.summary: We study the absolute open-strangeness density $n_{|S|}$ of strongly interacting matter at vanishing conserved-charge chemical potentials. Unlike the net-strangeness susceptibility $χ_2^S$, this quantity is not a derivative of the QCD partition function and requires a microscopic specification of the strangeness carriers. We use an equation of state that interpolates between an interacting hadron resonance gas and a quark-gluon plasma, with parameters fixed previously by lattice-QCD bulk thermodynamics. The ratio of $n_{|S|}$ to the entropy density $s$ follows the hadron-gas behavior below $T\simeq120$ MeV, rises above the ideal massless $2+1$-flavor limit of approximately $0.053$ across the crossover, and approaches this limit from above at high temperature. The same equation of state, minimally extended to finite $μ_S$, captures the temperature dependence of the lattice-QCD $χ_2^S$. For uncorrelated singly-strange Boltzmann particles, the strangeness fluctuation factor $F_S=χ_2^S/(n_{|S|}/T^3)$ equals unity. Within the constructed equation of state, it deviates from unity by less than $10\%$. This allows us to estimate $n_{|S|}/s$ from lattice-QCD data on $χ_2^S$ and $s$. The lattice-based estimate reaches a maximum of $n_{|S|}/s\simeq0.063$ at $T\simeq220$ MeV, followed by a $20\%$ decrease towards the high-temperature limit.

papers.title: Long-Term Quantile Treatment Effects with Combined Experimental and Observational Data
papers.summary: This paper studies the identification, estimation, and inference of long-term quantile treatment effects (LTQTEs) when short-term experimental data are supplemented with long-term observational data. Under a latent unconfoundedness framework, we establish identification of the LTQTE curve and derive the corresponding efficient influence functions. Building on these influence functions, we propose a semiparametrically efficient estimation procedure and develop a multiplier bootstrap method for uniform inference on the LTQTE curve, yielding valid simultaneous confidence bands over a continuum of quantile indices.

papers.title: Milk yield responses to heat stress in tropical dairy cattle
papers.summary: Context: Rising temperatures and warm tropical nights threaten dairy productivity and resilience across tropical landscapes. Objective: This study characterises multi-scale interactions among thermal regimes, nighttime cooling, metabolic heat load, and crossbred genetics on daily milk yield in Brazilian dairy systems. Methods: A 24-year panel (2001--2024) of 788,528 test-day records from 87,809 Girolando (Holstein $\times$ Gyr) cows across 408 municipalities was linked to weather data. Two-way fixed effects, distributed lag, and piecewise threshold spline models were estimated across yield quartiles and crossbred fractions. Results: While aggregate summaries suggest stable yield up to a daily mean Temperature--Humidity Index (THI) of 76, production-stratified splines show high-yielding cows lose milk starting at THI 68 and accelerating above 76 ($-0.162$ kg animal$^{-1}$ d$^{-1}$ unit$^{-1}$, $p=0.0062$), whereas low-yielding cows remain unaffected ($p=0.81$). Distributed lag models reveal an immediate drop followed by a deeper trough four days later. Lack of nighttime relief ($\mathrm{THI}_{\min} \ge 68$) reduces yield by an extra 2.37 kg animal$^{-1}$ d$^{-1}$ ($p \le 0.001$) and causes an 8.6\% loss after seven warm nights, whereas wide diurnal amplitude buffers output by $+1.60$ kg animal$^{-1}$ d$^{-1}$. At comparable high yields ($\approx 31$ kg animal$^{-1}$ d$^{-1}$), intermediate crossbreds ($1/2$ and $5/8$ Holstein) sustain yield up to THI 76, whereas $7/8$ Holstein cows decline at THI 68. Conclusions: Tropical dairy adaptation requires continuous nighttime cooling for high-yielding cows combined with balanced Zebu--taurine crossbreeding.
authors: Marcos Vinicius Gualberto Barbosa da Silva

papers.title: A Predictive Nuclear Effective Field Theory from Wilsonian Renormalization Group Principles II: Hidden unitary transformations
papers.summary: A fundamental challenge in nuclear effective field theories (EFTs) is to demonstrate the equivalence of interactions built at different momentum cutoffs and calibrated to the same set of low-momentum observables. Focusing on contact terms, we explicitly construct the unitary transformation that connects these EFT Hamiltonians. By replacing the conventional \emph{relative}-momentum cutoff with a universal single-particle \emph{absolute}-momentum cutoff, we show that this transformation can be systematically implemented using the similarity renormalization group (SRG) technique. The key insight is that such a regularization scheme enables a manifest decoupling of the many-body Fock space, avoiding transitions of particles in intermediate states into high-momentum subspaces associated with conventional \emph{relative}-momentum regulators. The derivation closely parallels the momentum-shell integration formalism of the Wilsonian RG flow. Reformulating the path integral in terms of unitary transformations allows a more intuitive, energy-independent analysis of nonrelativistic many-body systems within the EFT framework. In particular, this framework ensures that effective interactions calibrated in few-body sectors remain unitarily equivalent when applied to many-body systems, a central requirement not yet fulfilled in nuclear many-body calculations. We also show that the breaking of Galilean invariance due to the \emph{absolute}-momentum regularization induces irrelevant operators controlled by the RG scaling behavior, without introducing further complications. We numerically demonstrate our theoretical analysis using a one-dimensional toy model of bosons. These results provide a useful tool for analyzing the RG evolution of nonrelativistic many-body systems.

papers.title: SEAM: Computer-Use Agents Know the Harm Between Screens, and Commit It Anyway
papers.summary: Safety benchmarks for computer-use agents (CUAs) place the harm either in the intent of the task or on a single screen: a malicious instruction, an injected command, a phishing page. An agent that checks the task and each screen in isolation can pass them, so they do not test whether it combines facts seen on different screens. Yet in delegated work, harm often arises exactly this way: a fact about a person on one screen, a fact about an item on another, and a legitimate task that binds them. We introduce SEAM (Safety Execution Across Multiple screens), a benchmark of such cross-screen compositional harm: 600 multi-step, cross-application OSWorld tasks in which the instruction and every single observation are benign and only their combination is harmful. Minimal-pair variants that differ in one place, scored from the server log rather than by an LLM judge, locate where an agent fails. General-purpose open-weight and flagship agents carry out the harm in up to 92% of runs, yet decline when the user states it in one sentence. Agents open the decisive pages, so exposure is not the primary bottleneck. Asked about those pages, they flag the harm, and with thinking they often write the conflict into their reasoning and confirm anyway. Safety recognition thus does not reliably translate into safe execution, and the translation depends on the information channel: the same warning stops agents far more often in the user's instruction than on screen. Proprietary models are markedly more cautious. We release SEAM with its generator and quality gates at https://yuxuan2003.github.io/SEAM/ .

papers.title: A Minimal Toy Model of Charged Superradiant Spin-Down in Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals
papers.summary: Long-lived extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are sensitive to slow changes in the mass and spin of their central black holes. We construct a deliberately minimal toy model in which an effective hidden charge opens a charged-superradiance channel, a bosonic cloud grows from a seed, and energy and angular momentum are transferred from a rotating black hole to the cloud. The model is not a Kerr-Newman perturbation calculation. Instead, it consists of a threshold function, one phenomenological rate coefficient, and balance equations that conserve the combined black-hole-cloud energy. This reduction yields an analytic relation between mass loss and spin-down and makes the roles of the growth coefficient, seed energy, and superradiant margin transparent. For an illustrative system with initial mass $2\times10^6 M_\odot$, spin 0.90, effective charge-to-mass ratio 0.30, and a one-year evolution time, the chosen benchmark reaches $M/M_0=0.8933$ and $a_\star=0.7704$. These values are then passed to FastEMRIWaveforms as two stationary Kerr snapshots. The resulting figures show that the endpoint state has a shifted time-domain oscillation pattern and a lower-frequency harmonic structure relative to the initial state. Because the snapshots are regenerated independently, they do not constitute a phase-connected, time-dependent waveform and cannot by themselves support a detectability claim. The value of the construction is instead diagnostic: it isolates a compact set of assumptions, exposes parameter degeneracies, and identifies the minimum ingredients required for a future self-consistent calculation. In this sense, the model provides a reproducible bridge between charged-superradiance intuition and EMRI waveform studies without presenting its benchmark as an astrophysical forecast.

papers.title: Shell crossing and the dynamical formation of thin shells in the collapse of self-gravitating relativistic dust
papers.summary: In this paper, we show that shell crossing in the collapse of self-gravitating relativistic dust in spherical symmetry can be understood as dynamical formation of a thin shell of dust. More precisely, we consider the spherically symmetric Einstein-dust system in double null coordinates (E-d), for which first singularities with area radius bounded away from zero are known as 'shell crossing' singularities. We show that there exists a weak solution of (E-d), in which a thin shell of dust forms, extending beyond any 'non-degenerate' first shell crossing singularity of a smooth 'collapsing' solution of (E-d). This local extension is unique in the class of piecewise smooth solutions of (E-d) satisfying a 'determinism condition'. We then consider the physical problem of smooth data for (E-d) on an initial hypersurface diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$, containing a collapsing dust cloud. We show that, for generic such initial data, there exists a maximal globally hyperbolic piecewise smooth development satisfying a 'propagation condition' (stronger than the determinism condition). The development may contain an arbitrary (finite) number of thin shells which can moreover merge. All shell crossing singularities are 'resolved' and the area radius extends continuously to zero at any first singularity of the maximal development. We note that, for an open set of initial data in the smooth topology, as shown by Christodoulou, a Cauchy horizon emanates from a central 'shell-focussing' singularity.

papers.title: A Predictive Nuclear Effective Field Theory from Wilsonian Renormalization Group Principles I: Medium-mass nuclei and nuclear matter
papers.summary: The predictive power of nuclear effective field theory (EFT) from few- to many-body systems is substantially restricted by regulator dependence. Wilsonian momentum-shell renormalization group (RG) offers a natural framework for cutoff-independent predictions, but its many-body implementation requires regulating single-particle momentum modes, which breaks Galilean invariance. RG scaling analysis shows that this symmetry breaking is encoded in irrelevant operators whose effects can be included explicitly or absorbed into higher-body interactions. Guided by Wilsonian RG, we construct a regularization scheme for chiral EFT contact interactions and predict binding energies of nuclei up to $^{40}$Ca using interactions calibrated only to $A\leq3$ systems. The predicted energies vary at the percent level and agree with experiment for $300\leqΛ\leq450$~MeV. The same scheme reduces the overbinding of symmetric nuclear matter obtained with conventional relative-momentum regulators. Our results suggest that some model dependence observed in nonrelativistic many-body calculations originates from treating EFT vertices as static, Galilean-invariant potentials rather than as field operators regulated consistently across particle-number sectors.

papers.title: Sim2CBF: From Forward Simulations to Implicit Control Barrier Function Safety Filtering without Model Derivatives
papers.summary: Failure avoidance in complex robot-environment interactions is challenging because the underlying dynamics are difficult to model accurately, and available predictive models may not provide reliable derivatives. We present Sim2CBF, a failure-avoidance framework that solves the Control Barrier Function (CBF)-Safety Filter (SF) optimization problem using only forward-model evaluations, thereby avoiding differentiation of the predictive model. Specifically, we approximate the CBF constraint using finite differences and local linear interpolation over sampled control inputs while preserving failure-avoidance guarantees. The underlying CBF is implicit and constructed from backup-policy rollouts, enabling the use of expressive predictive models such as physics-based simulators and learned world models. Compared with purely sampling-based SFs, our formulation requires fewer control samples and yields less conservative behavior than direct nominal-backup blending. We evaluate Sim2CBF in simulation, hardware box-toppling, and vision-based control tasks, demonstrating its applicability to contact-rich and learned dynamics, as well as its adaptability to changes in the predictive model.

papers.title: Fiberpose: state-of-the-art fiber morphometry and instance segmentation with a distance-transform neural network
papers.summary: Analysis of fibrous structures in SEM images is a routine task in biomedical engineering and materials science. However, most available methods for fiber quantification still rely on classical image binarization followed by simple post-processing. These approaches often produce unreliable results in images with weak boundaries, heterogeneous contrast, and densely packed fibers. Here, we introduce Fiberpose, a framework that reformulates fiber analysis as direct regression of a smooth distance-transform (DT) field, together with a novel set of geometry-based algorithms specifically adapted to this representation. The predicted field directly encodes fiber geometry, while the accompanying algorithms enable instance reconstruction and measurement of diameter and orientation within a unified workflow. The framework is implemented as a standalone Python desktop application and a web tool https://fiberpose.org. On an independent dataset of fibrous SEM images, Fiberpose achieved state-of-the-art instance-segmentation accuracy in comparison with SAM2 and Cellpose-SAM, and more accurate diameter measurements than DiameterJ, Fibar and GIFT. The method remains effective in dense and weakly contrasted regions and shows qualitative generalization across microscopy modalities not represented in the training data. Fiberpose therefore provides an interpretable geometric representation and an automated pipeline for reproducible quantitative characterization of fibrous materials.

papers.title: A high-dimensional spatial-physical coupling operator for generalizable super-resolution of three-dimensional turbulent flows
papers.summary: Accurate representation of turbulent flows requires simultaneously capturing multi-scale spatial structures and the complex, nonlinear coupling between distinct physical quantities (\textit{e.g.}, velocity components and density). In practice, however, turbulent data are often constrained by low spatial resolution due to hardware limitations and computational costs. While current data-driven super-resolution methods have shown promise by learning mappings via convolutional neural networks (CNNs), they typically treat physical variables as independent channels. This simplified approach neglects intrinsic cross-variable correlations, causing models to struggle with high-fidelity reconstruction, particularly under extremely sparse conditions or in out-of-distribution regimes. To bridge this gap, we propose an architecture-agnostic spatial-physical coupling operator that extends the standard convolution into a joint spatial-variable dimension. Unlike conventional linear channel mixing, our framework constructs a unified spatial-physical representation within CNNs to explicitly capture local inter-variable interactions. By lifting features into a higher-dimensional manifold, this operator significantly enhances the model's representation capacity. Experiments demonstrate that this approach enables strong reconstruction performance and zero-shot generalization, offering a physics-aware inductive bias for super-resolution of three-dimensional turbulence. More broadly, this work suggests that high-dimensional operators offer a promising avenue for modeling intricate multi-scale turbulent flows.

papers.title: Universal Mass Equation for Equal-Quantum Excited-States Sets~III
papers.summary: Using our simple logarithmic Universal Mass Equation, we considered heavy non-$q\bar{q}$ meson states. PDG2026 reported a series of mesons with quantum numbers not allowed for standard $q\bar{q}$ states. Using LQCD predictions, we evaluated a scalar $0^{++}$ and tensor $2^{++}$ glueball series for which predictions are available. This approach allows us to predict heavy states that require future experimental studies. Additionally, we consider the possible misidentification of some meson states.

papers.title: Probing the Macroscopic Imprints of Singularity Resolution: Polarization Diagnostics of Rotating ABG Black Holes
papers.summary: Recent observations by the Event Horizon Telescope have revealed important electromagnetic information around the supermassive black holes $\text{M87}^*$ and $\text{Sgr A}^*$, providing experimental supports for investigating physics near the event horizon. In the absence of a complete quantum gravity theory, exploring the observational appearances and polarized images of accretion flows in regularized geometries, and seeking specific observational differences from Kerr black holes, is of value for understanding the singularity problem. Based on backward ray tracing method, this work investigates both the optical and polarimetric observational features of rotating Ayón-Beato-García spacetime with regularization parameter $Q$. It is found that, compared with the Kerr case, the parameter $Q$ leads to a significant contraction of the size of the inner shadow in the observed optical images. This contraction remains visible even after an illustrative Gaussian filter for images observed at a low inclination angle (e.g. $17^\circ$). In the polarized images, we focus on two observables, the electric vector position angles (EVPAs) and the depolarization regions, on the observer's screen. It is found that depolarization regions do not necessarily reside in the vicinity of the bright photon ring in images at high inclination angles (e.g. $83^\circ$), and a multi-branch structure can be observed. Furthermore, the distribution of EVPAs is insensitive to the regularization parameter $Q$ while the morphology of the depolarization regions can be impacted remarkably by $Q$. The results provide possible optical observable characteristics for the rotating regular spacetime.

papers.title: JALE: A new Python toolbox for coordinate-based neuroimaging meta-analysis using activation likelihood estimation
papers.summary: Coordinate-based neuroimaging meta-analysis using activation likelihood estimation (ALE) is commonly used to synthesize reported results of functional or structural magnetic resonance imaging studies. We here present JALE, a new, open-source Python package for conducting ALE meta-analyses. Besides computing standard ALE main effects and contrast analyses, this toolbox implements several novel analytical approaches including new options for thresholding (threshold-free cluster enhancement statistics, significance threshold prediction) as well as sensitivity and cluster analyses that were only available as in-house scripts in the past. The purpose of this paper is to provide an integrated conceptual foundation of recent developments in the ALE meta-analysis framework, with a particular focus on novel methodological implementations that can be executed in a straightforward and standardized manner using the new JALE toolbox.

papers.title: Sideslip-Conditioned Drift Trajectory Planning with Flow Matching and Control Barrier Functions
papers.summary: Drifting, the deliberate control of a vehicle at large sideslip angles, is relevant to both motorsport and recovery from unexpected oversteer. Existing autonomous drifting methods typically determine drift intensity through predefined reference trajectories, optimization objectives, or learned policy rewards, rather than accepting a desired sideslip angle as an explicit input. We propose, to the best of our knowledge, the first generative drift trajectory planner explicitly conditioned on a requested peak sideslip angle. A conditional flow matching model is trained on demonstrated drift laps with hindsight-derived sideslip labels and refined through reinforcement fine-tuning. A control barrier function (CBF) correction is then applied to satisfy model-based road, tire friction, and actuator constraints at the planning waypoints. In closed-loop experiments in the racing simulator Assetto Corsa, a nonlinear model predictive controller tracks the generated plans for six requested sideslip angles from 20 deg to 45 deg, with 30 laps (approximately 75 km) per request. The median peak sideslip angle measured across drift-corner passes follows the requested angle, with a mean absolute error of 1.2 deg across the six conditions.
